ae_data.cfg.mon.N.lvl.manualText: The master output level control for the monitor path. This parameter adjusts the overall volume of the monitor mix, allowing you to set the desired listening level for performers or engineers using the monitor system. Adjusting this control will affect the output level of all channels routed to this monitor path.

ae_data.cfg.mon.N.inv.manualText: This parameter indicates whether the phase of the audio signal for this monitor path is inverted. When enabled, the polarity of the signal is flipped, which can be useful for correcting phase issues in the audio or for creative effects. Phase inversion can help to reduce feedback or to align the phase of multiple signals when they are combined in the monitor mix.

ae_data.cfg.mon.N.pan.manualText: The pan control for the monitor path, which allows you to adjust the stereo positioning of the audio signal. By moving the pan control left or right, you can create a sense of space and separation in the monitor mix, helping performers to better hear their own signal or other elements in the mix. The pan parameter typically ranges from full left to full right, with a center position that provides an equal balance of the left and right channels.

ae_data.cfg.mon.N.wid.manualText: The stereo width control for the monitor path, which allows you to adjust the perceived width of the stereo image. Increasing the width can make the audio sound more spacious and immersive, while decreasing it can create a more focused and centered sound. This parameter can be used to enhance the clarity of individual elements in the monitor mix or to create a more enveloping listening experience for performers.

ae_data.cfg.mon.N.eq.on.manualText: This parameter indicates whether the equalizer (EQ) for this path is active. When enabled, the EQ settings for this channel will be applied to the audio signal, allowing you to shape the tonal balance of the monitor mix. The EQ can be used to boost or cut specific frequency ranges, helping performers to better hear certain elements in the mix or to reduce unwanted frequencies that may cause feedback or muddiness.

ae_data.cfg.mon.N.eq.lsg.manualText: The gain control for the low-shelf filter, which allows you to adjust the amount of boost or cut applied to frequencies below the cutoff frequency. This parameter can be used to shape the low-end response of the monitor mix, helping to emphasize or reduce certain frequency ranges as needed.

ae_data.cfg.mon.N.eq.lsf.manualText: The cutoff frequency for the low-shelf filter, which determines the point at which the filter begins to attenuate or boost frequencies. This parameter can be used to shape the low-end response of the monitor mix, helping to emphasize or reduce certain frequency ranges as needed.

ae_data.cfg.mon.N.lim.manualText: The threshold level for the limiter on the monitor path. When the audio signal exceeds this level, the limiter will engage to prevent clipping and distortion, ensuring that the output remains clean and undistorted even during loud passages. Adjusting this parameter allows you to set the maximum output level for the monitor mix, providing protection for both the equipment and the listeners' ears.

ae_data.cfg.mon.N.dly.on.manualText: The switch to activate or deactivate the delay on the monitor path.

ae_data.cfg.mon.N.dly.m.labelText: Delay Time (meters, feet, milliseconds or number of samples)
ae_data.cfg.mon.N.dly.m.manualText: The delay time for the monitor path, which can be set in various units such as meters, feet, milliseconds, or number of samples. This parameter allows you to create a sense of space and depth in the monitor mix by introducing a slight delay to the audio signal. Adjusting the delay time can help performers to better hear themselves or other elements in the mix, especially in larger venues where sound reflections can cause timing issues.

ae_data.cfg.mon.N.dim.manualText: The dim control for the monitor path, which allows you to reduce the overall volume of the monitor mix by a specified amount. This can be useful for quickly lowering the volume when communicating with performers or when you need to temporarily reduce the level without changing the main output level. The dim attenuation level is typically set in decibels (dB) and can be adjusted to achieve the desired amount of reduction.

ae_data.cfg.mon.N.pfldim.manualText: The PFL (Pre-Fade Listen) dim control for the monitor path, which allows you to reduce the volume of the PFL signal by a specified amount. This can be useful for quickly lowering the level of the PFL signal when cueing up channels or when you need to temporarily reduce the level without affecting the main output. The PFL dim attenuation level is typically set in decibels (dB) and can be adjusted to achieve the desired amount of reduction.

ae_data.cfg.mon.N.eqbdtrim.manualText: The global EQ band trim override control for the monitor path, which allows you to adjust the gain of each EQ band independently. This can be useful for fine-tuning the frequency response of the monitor mix and addressing specific frequency issues.

ae_data.cfg.mon.N.srclvl.manualText: The level control for the direct input source in the monitor path. This parameter allows you to adjust the volume of the audio signal coming from a direct input source, such as a microphone or instrument, that is routed to the monitor mix. Adjusting this control can help performers to better hear their own signal or other elements in the mix that are coming from direct inputs.

ae_data.cfg.mon.N.srcmix.manualText: The mix level adjustment control for the direct input source in the monitor path. This parameter allows you to balance the contribution of the direct input signal within the overall monitor mix.

ae_data.cfg.mon.N.src.manualText: The primary tap signal source for the monitor path, which determines the point in the signal flow from which the audio is taken for monitoring. This can include options such as pre-fader, post-fader, or post-EQ taps, allowing you to choose the most appropriate signal source for the monitor mix based on your needs and preferences.

ae_data.cfg.mon.N.dirin.manualText: The route path for the direct input source in the monitor path. This parameter allows you to specify which input channel or bus the direct input signal should be routed to for monitoring.

ae_data.cfg.mon.N.tags.manualText: Custom tags that can be assigned to the monitor path for organizational or identification purposes. These tags can be used to label the monitor path with specific information, such as the name of the performer or the type of signal being monitored, making it easier to manage and navigate the monitor mix during a live performance or recording session.

ae_data.cfg.solo.mode.manualText: The configuration for the behavior of the solo mode in the monitor path. This parameter allows you to define how the solo functionality operates, such as whether it mutes other channels or just focuses on the soloed channel.

ae_data.cfg.solo.mon.manualText: The assigned monitor path target for the solo function. This parameter allows you to specify which monitor path will be affected when a channel is soloed, ensuring that the soloed signal is routed to the appropriate monitor mix for listening.

ae_data.cfg.solo.mute.manualText: The override control for muting individual channels in the monitor path. This parameter allows you to manually mute specific channels, which can be useful for troubleshooting or during live performances.

ae_data.cfg.solo.chtap.manualText: The tap point for the channel solo function, which determines the point in the signal flow from which the soloed audio is taken. This can include options such as pre-fader, post-fader, or post-EQ taps, allowing you to choose the most appropriate signal source for the solo function based on your needs and preferences.

ae_data.cfg.solo.bustap.manualText: The tap point for the bus solo function, which determines the point in the signal flow from which the soloed audio is taken. This can include options such as pre-fader, post-fader, or post-EQ taps, allowing you to choose the most appropriate signal source for the solo function based on your needs and preferences.

ae_data.cfg.solo.maintap.manualText: The tap point for the main solo function, which determines the point in the signal flow from which the soloed audio is taken. This can include options such as pre-fader, post-fader, or post-EQ taps, allowing you to choose the most appropriate signal source for the solo function based on your needs and preferences.

ae_data.cfg.solo.mtxtap.manualText: The tap point for the matrix solo function, which determines the point in the signal flow from which the soloed audio is taken. This can include options such as pre-fader, post-fader, or post-EQ taps, allowing you to choose the most appropriate signal source for the solo function based on your needs and preferences.

ae_data.cfg.solo.srcsolo.manualText: The source channel for the solo bus function, which determines which channel's audio will be sent to the solo bus when a channel is soloed. This parameter allows you to specify the source of the soloed signal, ensuring that the correct audio is routed to the solo bus for listening.

ae_data.cfg.rta.rtarange.manualText: The dynamic range span for the RTA meter, which determines the minimum and maximum values that the meter will display. This parameter allows you to adjust the sensitivity of the RTA meter to better visualize the audio signal. A wider range can help to capture both very quiet and very loud signals, while a narrower range can provide more detail for signals that fall within a specific level.

ae_data.cfg.rta.rtagain.manualText: The input gain for the RTA meter, which adjusts the level of the incoming signal before it is processed by the meter. This parameter allows you to optimize the meter's performance for different input levels. Increasing the gain can help to make quieter signals more visible on the meter, while decreasing it can prevent louder signals from overloading the meter and causing it to max out.

ae_data.cfg.rta.rtaauto.manualText: The auto-gain adjustment for the RTA meter, which automatically adjusts the gain based on the incoming signal level. This parameter allows you to maintain a consistent display level without manual intervention.

ae_data.cfg.rta.eqdecay.manualText: The decay speed for the EQ screen, which determines how quickly the display updates to reflect changes in the audio signal. This parameter allows you to adjust the responsiveness of the EQ display to better visualize the audio characteristics. A faster decay speed can provide a more real-time representation of the audio signal, while a slower decay speed can create a smoother, more averaged display that may be easier to read in certain situations.

ae_data.cfg.rta.eqdet.manualText: The detection type for the EQ meter, which determines how the meter responds to the incoming audio signal. This parameter allows you to choose between different detection methods, such as peak or RMS, to better visualize the audio characteristics. Peak detection responds to the highest level of the signal, while RMS detection provides an average level over time. Choosing the appropriate detection type can help you to better understand the dynamics of the audio signal and make informed decisions about adjustments.

ae_data.cfg.rta.eqrange.manualText: The dynamic range for the EQ analyzer, which determines the minimum and maximum values that the analyzer will display. This parameter allows you to adjust the sensitivity of the EQ analyzer to better visualize the audio signal. A wider range can help to capture both very quiet and very loud signals, while a narrower range can provide more detail for signals that fall within a specific level. Adjusting the EQ analyzer dynamic range can help you to better understand the frequency content of the audio signal and make informed decisions about EQ adjustments.

ae_data.cfg.rta.eqgain.manualText: The gain adjustment for the EQ grid calibration, which allows you to fine-tune the sensitivity of the EQ analyzer to better visualize the audio signal. This parameter is typically used to ensure accurate representation of the audio characteristics across different input levels. Adjusting the EQ grid calibration gain can help you to achieve a more accurate and useful display of the frequency content of the audio signal, allowing for more informed decisions about EQ adjustments.

ae_data.cfg.rta.eqauto.manualText: The auto-range adjustment for the EQ meter, which automatically adjusts the display scale based on the incoming audio signal. This parameter allows you to maintain a consistent visualization of the audio characteristics without manual intervention. When enabled, the EQ meter will dynamically adjust its scale to accommodate changes in the signal level, ensuring that the display remains informative and easy to read across a wide range of input levels.

ae_data.cfg.mtr.scopesrc.manualText: The source for the oscilloscope input trigger, which determines when the oscilloscope captures and displays the audio signal. This parameter allows you to select the appropriate trigger source based on your specific needs and the characteristics of the audio signal. Common trigger sources include the main output, a specific bus, or a direct input channel. Choosing the right trigger source can help you to achieve a stable and informative display on the oscilloscope, allowing you to analyze the waveform of the audio signal effectively.

ae_data.cfg.mtr.scopetap.manualText: The point at which the oscilloscope taps into the audio signal for display. This parameter allows you to select the specific location in the signal chain where the oscilloscope will capture and display the waveform. Choosing the appropriate tap point can help you to analyze different aspects of the audio signal effectively. Common tap points include pre-fader, post-fader, or post-EQ, each providing a different perspective on the signal's characteristics. Adjusting the oscilloscope tap point can help you to better understand the behavior of the audio signal at various stages of processing.

ae_data.cfg.mtr.mtrsfc.in.manualText: The patch for the input local preamp, which allows you to adjust the gain and other parameters for the input signal before it reaches the main processing chain. This parameter is typically used to ensure proper signal levels and to apply any necessary preprocessing to the audio signal. Adjusting the input local preamp patch can help you to optimize the sound quality and ensure that the signal is properly prepared for further processing in the mixer.

ae_data.cfg.mtr.mtrsfc.bus.manualText: The routing configuration for the bus send matrix, which determines how the audio signal is distributed to different buses within the mixing environment. This parameter allows you to create complex signal paths and manage the flow of audio between various processing stages. By adjusting the bus send matrix routing, you can control which buses receive the audio signal and how it is processed, enabling you to create customized mixes and effects for different channels or groups of channels.

By adjusting the main mix send routing, you can control which channels receive the audio signal and how it is processed, enabling you to create tailored mixes for different listening scenarios.

Common options for the main level meter target include the main output, a specific bus, or a direct input channel. By selecting the right target for the main level meter, you can ensure that you are monitoring the most relevant audio signal for your needs, allowing you to make informed decisions about adjustments and maintain optimal sound quality.

By selecting the right position mode for the main metering tap, you can ensure that you are monitoring the most relevant audio signal for your needs, allowing you to make informed decisions about adjustments and maintain optimal sound quality.

ae_data.cfg.talk.assign.manualText: The channel currently selected on the control surface for editing and monitoring. This parameter allows you to focus on a specific channel and make adjustments to its settings. By selecting a channel on the control surface, you can access its parameters and make changes as needed, allowing for efficient and precise control over the audio mix. The current control surface selected channel is typically displayed on the control surface itself, providing visual feedback to the user about which channel is being edited.

ae_data.cfg.talk.lvl.manualText: The volume level for the master output, which controls the overall loudness of the mixed audio signal. This parameter allows you to adjust the output level to match the requirements of your listening environment or the capabilities of your playback system. By setting the master output volume appropriately, you can ensure that the audio is delivered at a comfortable and consistent level for listeners. It is important to monitor the master output volume to avoid clipping and distortion, while also ensuring that the audio is loud enough for the intended audience.

ae_data.cfg.talk.N.mode.manualText: The behavior of the solo mode, which determines how the audio signal is processed when a channel is soloed. This parameter allows you to configure the solo mode to suit your mixing preferences and workflow. Common options for the solo mode include pre-fader, post-fader, or other specialized solo behaviors. By selecting the right solo mode, you can ensure that the audio signal is processed in a way that meets your creative and technical requirements.

ae_data.cfg.talk.N.mondim.manualText: The dimming status for the main stage monitor, which controls the brightness of the display. This parameter allows you to adjust the monitor brightness to match the lighting conditions of your environment or the capabilities of your display system. By setting the monitor dim status appropriately, you can ensure that the display is visible and comfortable for users. It is important to monitor the monitor dim status to avoid glare and eye strain, while also ensuring that the display is bright enough for the intended audience.

ae_data.cfg.talk.N.busdim.manualText: The dimming level for the secondary bus path, which controls the brightness of the display for that specific path. This parameter allows you to adjust the monitor brightness to match the lighting conditions of your environment or the capabilities of your display system. By setting the bus dim status appropriately, you can ensure that the display is visible and comfortable for users. It is important to monitor the bus dim status to avoid glare and eye strain, while also ensuring that the display is bright enough for the intended audience.  This parameter is typically used to optimize the visibility of the display for different bus paths, allowing you to create a more comfortable and efficient working environment for users.

ae_data.cfg.talk.N.indiv.manualText: The metering behavior for individual channels, which determines how the audio signal is displayed on the control surface. This parameter allows you to configure the metering to suit your mixing preferences and workflow. Common options for the metering include peak, RMS, or other specialized metering behaviors. By selecting the right metering option, you can ensure that the audio signal is displayed in a way that meets your creative and technical requirements.  This parameter is typically used to optimize the visibility of the audio signal for individual channels, allowing you to make informed decisions about adjustments and maintain optimal sound quality.

ae_data.cfg.amix.x.manualText: AUTOMIX has independent switches to enable the X and Y groups for Automix processing. When the X group is enabled, the X parameter serves as the primary dynamic control for the Automix algorithm, influencing how the system attenuates channels based on their relative levels and activity. The Y parameter can be used in conjunction to provide additional dynamic shaping, but the X parameter is typically the main driver of the Automix behavior.

ae_data.cfg.amix.y.manualText: AUTOMIX has independent switches to enable the X and Y groups for Automix processing. When the Y group is enabled, the Y parameter provides an additional layer of dynamic control that can interact with the X parameter to further refine the Automix algorithm's response. The Y parameter can be used to influence factors such as how quickly channels are attenuated or how the system responds to changes in channel activity, allowing for more nuanced control over the overall mix.

ae_data.io.altsw.manualText: The alternate input source switch allows you to toggle between the primary and alternate input sources for a given channel. This parameter is typically used to quickly switch between different audio sources, such as a microphone and a line input, without having to reconfigure the entire signal path. By using the alternate input source switch, you can easily manage multiple audio sources and ensure that the correct signal is being processed and monitored at any given time.

ae_data.io.autoaltovr.manualText: The auto alternate input override function automatically switches to the alternate input source when certain conditions are met, such as when the primary input signal falls below a specified threshold. This parameter allows you to ensure that audio is maintained even if the primary source experiences issues, providing a seamless transition to the alternate source without manual intervention. By enabling auto alternate input override, you can enhance the reliability of your audio system and minimize disruptions during live performances or critical recording sessions.

ae_data.io.in.LCL.N.mode.manualText: The behavior of the solo mode for the local input channel, which determines how the audio signal is processed when the channel is soloed. This parameter allows you to configure the solo mode to suit your mixing preferences and workflow. Common options for the solo mode include pre-fader, post-fader, or other specialized solo behaviors. By selecting the right solo mode, you can ensure that the audio signal is processed in a way that meets your creative and technical requirements when soloing the channel.

ae_data.io.in.LCL.N.g.manualText: The analog preamp input gain controls the amplification of the analog audio signal before it is processed by the digital components of the system. Adjusting this parameter allows you to optimize the signal level for the best performance and minimize noise or distortion in your mix. By setting the appropriate gain level, you can ensure that the audio signal is strong enough to be processed effectively while avoiding clipping or other issues that can arise from excessive gain. This parameter is typically used to fine-tune the input signal for optimal sound quality and performance in the mixing environment.

ae_data.io.in.LCL.N.vph.manualText: The +48V phantom power status indicates whether the channel is receiving phantom power from the audio interface. This parameter is typically used to manage the power supply to condenser microphones and other equipment that requires phantom power for operation. By monitoring the phantom power status, you can ensure that your microphones and other devices are receiving the necessary power to function properly, and you can troubleshoot any issues related to phantom power supply. This parameter is important for maintaining optimal performance and sound quality in your audio setup, especially when using condenser microphones that rely on phantom power for their operation.

ae_data.io.in.LCL.N.mute.manualText: The channel mute override allows you to temporarily silence the channel without affecting the overall mute status. This parameter is typically used to isolate specific channels for troubleshooting or to prevent them from interfering with other elements in the mix. By enabling the channel mute override, you can quickly and easily manage the audio signal for that channel without having to adjust the main mute settings, providing greater flexibility and control over your mix. This parameter is especially useful in live sound situations or during recording sessions where quick adjustments may be necessary to maintain optimal sound quality.

ae_data.io.in.LCL.N.pol.manualText: The phase polarity flip parameter allows you to reverse the phase of the audio signal for the channel. By flipping the phase, you can adjust the way the audio signal interacts with other signals in the mix, potentially improving the overall sound quality or achieving a desired sonic effect. This parameter is typically used when you encounter phase cancellation issues, where two or more audio signals are out of phase and cause a reduction in sound quality. By flipping the phase of one of the signals, you can help to restore the balance and improve the clarity of the audio. Additionally, phase flipping can be used creatively to achieve unique sound textures or effects in your mix.

ae_data.ch.N.in.set.srcauto.manualText: Configures the automatic input source selection behavior for the channel. When enabled, this feature allows the system to automatically switch between primary and backup input sources based on signal presence or specific error conditions, ensuring uninterrupted audio playback and signal continuity.

ae_data.ch.N.in.set.altsrc.manualText: Defines the secondary or backup input source assigned to the channel configuration. This alternate source serves as a redundant failover option that the channel can quickly switch to if the primary input connection loses signal or encounters technical issues.

ae_data.ch.N.in.set.inv.manualText: Toggles or displays the phase (polarity) inversion status of the input signal. Engaging phase inversion flips the audio waveform 180 degrees, which is crucial for correcting phase cancellation issues when combining multiple microphones or audio sources capturing the same instrument.

ae_data.ch.N.in.set.trim.manualText: Adjusts the digital trim gain or attenuation level applied directly to the incoming signal. This parameter allows you to fine-tune and balance the input levels across different channels before the signal hits the main gain stages or mixing bus, preventing digital clipping.

ae_data.ch.N.in.set.bal.manualText: Controls the stereo balance and physical width positioning of a stereo audio source within the soundstage. Adjusting this parameter shifts the relative level between the left and right channels or alters the stereo field width, helping to place the audio signal precisely in the mix.

ae_data.ch.N.in.set.dlymode.manualText: Sets the preferred measurement unit used to calculate and display the channel delay. You can toggle this mode between different units such as milliseconds (ms), meters (m), feet (ft), or samples, allowing for intuitive adjustments depending on whether you are time-aligning speakers or phase-aligning microphones.

ae_data.ch.N.in.set.dly.manualText: Determines the exact amount of time delay applied to the channel's input signal. This parameter is used for precise time alignment, ensuring that audio signals from different physical distances arrive at the mixing position or listener's ears at the exact same moment to eliminate comb filtering.

ae_data.ch.N.in.set.dlyon.manualText: Enables or disables the delay processing stage for the channel. Toggling this parameter to the active state applies the configured time alignment delay value to the audio path, while turning it off completely bypasses the delay processing block.

ae_data.ch.N.in.conn.grp.manualText: Assigns the channel to a specific control or link group, such as a stereo pair or multi-channel gang. When designated to a link group, specific parameters like fader levels, mutes, or processing settings can be adjusted simultaneously across all grouped channels for simplified mixing workflow.

ae_data.ch.N.in.conn.in.manualText: Specifies the physical or digital hardware routing path for the local microphone preamplifier assigned to this channel. This parameter allows you to patch a specific hardware input jack to the internal software processing channel of the audio system.

ae_data.ch.N.in.conn.altgrp.manualText: Designates the channel to an alternative safe group configuration, such as a Mute Safe or VCA Safe group. This ensures that when global system commands or scene recalls are executed, the parameters of the channels within this safe group remain unaffected and isolated.

ae_data.ch.N.in.conn.altin.manualText: Determines the specific routing index or hardware address for an alternative preamplifier input channel. This parameter allows the system to reference a secondary hardware input patch, making it easy to hot-swap input signals or toggle between distinct hardware configurations.

ae_data.ch.N.flt.lc.manualText: Sets the static corner frequency for the Low-Cut (High-Pass) filter on the channel. Audio frequencies falling below this established limit will be rolled off, which helps eliminate problematic low-end rumble, stage vibration, mic handling noise, and unwanted proximity effect.

ae_data.ch.N.flt.lcf.manualText: Defines the dynamically controlled center or target frequency for the Low-Cut filter circuit. Unlike a static filter, this parameter represents the shifting operational point of an active high-pass filter that can adjust dynamically based on incoming signal energy or modulation inputs.

ae_data.ch.N.flt.lcs.manualText: Controls the attenuation slope steepness of the Low-Cut filter, measured in decibels per octave (dB/Oct). A higher value creates a much sharper, aggressive cut that rapidly rejects frequencies below the filter limit, while a lower value provides a smoother, more gradual roll-off.

ae_data.ch.N.flt.hc.manualText: Sets the static corner frequency for the High-Cut (Low-Pass) filter on the channel. Audio frequencies falling above this established limit will be rolled off, which helps eliminate high-frequency hiss, unwanted cymbal bleed, and digital harshness while smoothing the overall response.

ae_data.ch.N.flt.hcf.manualText: Defines the dynamically controlled center or target frequency for the High-Cut filter circuit. Unlike a static filter, this parameter represents the shifting operational point of an active low-pass filter that can adjust dynamically based on incoming signal energy or modulation inputs.

ae_data.ch.N.flt.hcs.manualText: Controls the attenuation slope steepness of the High-Cut filter, measured in decibels per octave (dB/Oct). A higher value creates a much sharper, aggressive cut that rapidly rejects frequencies above the filter limit, while a lower value provides a smoother, more gradual roll-off.

ae_data.ch.N.flt.tf.manualText: Displays or toggles the status of the True-Feedback Filter Mode. When activated, this specialized processing mode optimizes the channel filtering algorithms to suppress acoustic feedback loops in live sound environments without compromising the natural tonal balance of the source signal.

ae_data.ch.N.flt.mdl.manualText: Specifies the name or identifier of the digital insert effect model currently loaded into the channel processing slot. This parameter allows you to select and swap out various emulation models, such as vintage compressors, specific equalizers, or unique saturation modules.

ae_data.ch.N.flt.tilt.labelText: Tilt EQ Spectrum Balance Tone Shifter
ae_data.ch.N.flt.tilt.manualText: Adjusts the Tilt EQ parameter, which acts as a global tone shifter around a central pivot frequency. Boosting this parameter simultaneously raises high frequencies and attenuates low frequencies to brighten the signal, while cutting it dampens the highs and warms up the low end.

ae_data.ch.N.clink.manualText: Sets the status flag for linking adjacent channels into a coordinated stereo pair. When enabled, internal DSP parameters such as dynamics filters, EQ configurations, and gain settings are linked together, maintaining identical stereo processing symmetry across both channels.

ae_data.ch.N.col.labelText: Console Strip LCD Backlight Color Index
ae_data.ch.N.col.manualText: Determines the specific color index used for the physical console strip's LCD backlight display. This parameter allows you to color-code individual channels or channel types (e.g., vocals, drums, guitars) for quick visual identification on the hardware surface.

ae_data.ch.N.name.manualText: Stores the custom text string used to name or label the channel on the console scribblestrip and digital user interface. This parameter allows engineers to replace generic channel numbers with recognizable names for specific performers, instruments, or inputs.

ae_data.ch.N.icon.manualText: Selects the visual icon index code displayed on the channel's LCD screen. This parameter allows you to assign graphical icons (such as a microphone, guitar, or drum symbol) to the console strip, providing immediate visual confirmation of the channel content.

ae_data.ch.N.led.labelText: Physical Control Surface LED Accent Ring Switch
ae_data.ch.N.led.manualText: Controls the operational state of the physical LED accent ring surrounding the channel encoder on the hardware control surface. This switch can toggle the LED indicator behavior between standard parameter tracking modes, custom highlighting, or complete bypass.

ae_data.ch.N.mute.manualText: Engages the absolute mute override function for the channel. Activating this parameter instantly cuts the audio signal path at the designated mute stage, silencing the channel's output to the mixing buses without altering the underlying fader or gain positions.

ae_data.ch.N.fdr.manualText: Represents the exact volume or attenuation position value of the physical motorized fader on the control surface. Adjusting this parameter updates the level of the audio signal passing through the primary channel output stage and moves the physical hardware fader to match.

ae_data.ch.N.pan.manualText: The pan control for the channel path, which allows you to adjust the stereo positioning of the audio signal. By moving the pan control left or right, you can create a sense of space and separation in the main mix, helping to better position individual elements across the stereo field.

ae_data.ch.N.wid.manualText: Adjusts the perceived width of the stereo field for a stereo-linked channel. Modifying this control expands the stereo separation outward for a broader, more immersive soundstage, or narrows it down toward a focused center point to tighten the spatial positioning in the mix.

ae_data.ch.N.solosafe.manualText: Activates the Solo Safe mode for this channel. When enabled, this channel is isolated from the Solo-In-Place system, meaning it will not be muted when other channels on the console are soloed. This is ideal for effects returns, submixes, or critical ambient microphones.

ae_data.ch.N.mon.manualText: Sets the destination or target bus for the channel's monitor path routing. This parameter dictates where the channel's monitor mix signal is sent, allowing you to route specific audio feeds directly to performer headphones, stage wedges, or control room monitors.

ae_data.ch.N.proc.labelText: Internal Processing Core Algorithm Engine Routing
ae_data.ch.N.proc.manualText: Determines the internal routing path through the system's core digital signal processing (DSP) engine. This assigns the channel's audio data to a specific hardware processing core or virtual DSP algorithm bank to handle complex filtering, dynamics, and effects computations.

ae_data.ch.N.ptap.manualText: Selects the exact physical or logical location within the channel strip where the pre-processing signal is split off. This pickoff point captures the raw incoming audio before it passes through the channel's internal EQ, dynamics, or insert processing chains.

ae_data.ch.N.peq.on.manualText: Activates or deactivates the entire Parametric Equalizer (PEQ) module for the channel. Toggling this switch to the active position engages all configured EQ bands to shape the channel's tone, while turning it off completely bypasses the equalizer block.

ae_data.ch.N.peq.1g.manualText: Adjusts the gain level for the first band of the parametric equalizer. This parameter lets you boost or cut the amplitudes of the frequencies centered around Band 1, providing targeted tonal correction or filtering for the low or low-mid frequency spectrum.

ae_data.ch.N.peq.1f.manualText: Sets the center or corner frequency for the first band of the parametric equalizer. This parameter defines the exact point in the audio spectrum where Band 1's gain adjustments and Q-factor settings will be concentrated.

ae_data.ch.N.peq.1q.manualText: Controls the Q-factor (bandwidth) for the first band of the parametric equalizer. A higher Q-factor narrows the bandwidth for precise, surgical notches to eliminate problematic frequencies, while a lower Q-factor broadens the curve for smooth, natural sounding tonal boosts or cuts.

ae_data.ch.N.peq.2g.manualText: Adjusts the gain level for the second band of the parametric equalizer. This parameter allows you to boost or cut the audio signal at the frequency specified by Band 2, which is typically utilized for managing low-mid or mid-range instrumental and vocal characteristics.

ae_data.ch.N.peq.2f.manualText: Sets the center frequency for the second band of the parametric equalizer. This configuration establishes the operational midpoint in the mid-range spectrum where Band 2's boosting or cutting algorithms take effect.

ae_data.ch.N.peq.2q.manualText: Controls the Q-factor (bandwidth width) for the second band of the parametric equalizer. Adjusting this value alters how wide or narrow the frequency bell curve is around the Band 2 centerpoint, regulating how many surrounding mid-range frequencies are affected.

ae_data.ch.N.peq.3g.manualText: Adjusts the gain level for the third band of the parametric equalizer. This control boosts or cuts the signal levels across high-mid or high frequencies, allowing you to add presence, clarity, and brightness or reduce harshness in the channel signal.

ae_data.ch.N.peq.3f.manualText: Sets the center or corner frequency for the third band of the parametric equalizer. This parameter positions the filter's focus point in the upper-mid to high-frequency area of the audio spectrum for specialized top-end acoustic adjustments.

ae_data.ch.N.peq.3q.manualText: Controls the Q-factor (bandwidth response) for the third band of the parametric equalizer. Modifying this parameter dictates the sharpness of the high-mid or high filter curve, adapting it for either sweeping air/presence boosts or precise resonance taming.

ae_data.ch.N.gate.on.manualText: Activates or deactivates the noise gate/dynamics module for this channel. Enabling this switch puts the noise expander or gate processor into the signal path to silence unwanted low-level background bleed, while disabling it passes the audio unfiltered.

ae_data.ch.N.gate.mdl.manualText: Specifies the software emulation model or module style loaded into the channel's noise gate processing slot. This allows you to choose between various dynamic processing styles, such as classic hardware gates, clean digital expanders, or advanced modern downward expanders.

ae_data.ch.N.gate.mix.labelText: Dry/Wet Parallel Signal Effect Blending Percentage
ae_data.ch.N.gate.mix.manualText: Controls the blend percentage between the dry (unprocessed) and wet (gated/processed) audio signals. This parameter enables parallel dynamic processing, allowing you to retain natural signal transients and decay by mixing a portion of the original audio back into the gated output.

ae_data.ch.N.gate.gain.manualText: Adjusts the clean makeup gain level applied at the output stage of the gate/dynamics module. This parameter is used to normalize the channel volume and compensate for any overall level loss incurred during heavy dynamic attenuation or downward expansion.

ae_data.ch.N.gate.thr.manualText: Sets the threshold level for the gate's integrated compressor or sidechain detection logic. Audio signal peaks that cross above this designated decibel threshold will trigger the dynamics processor, dictating when the unit transitions between attenuation and unity gain.

ae_data.ch.N.gate.depth.manualText: Determines the maximum amount of signal attenuation applied when the noise gate or expander is fully closed. Also known as the floor range, a lower depth setting creates a subtle attenuation of background noise, while a maximum depth completely silences the signal path.

ae_data.ch.N.gate.fast.labelText: Dynamics Attack Profiler Fast-Response Mode Toggle
ae_data.ch.N.gate.fast.manualText: Toggles the fast-response mode for the dynamics processor's attack envelope analyzer. Engaging this feature forces the gate or compressor to react almost instantaneously to sudden, transient spikes (like drums or percussion), preventing the initial sound attack from being cut off.

ae_data.ch.N.gate.peak.manualText: Configures the peak ceiling detection threshold percentage for the processor's integrated limiting safety circuit. This parameter defines the absolute maximum peak limit allowed through the stage, triggering instant clamping if a transient threatens to introduce digital clipping.

ae_data.ch.N.gatesc.type.manualText: Selects the filter profile type utilized within the noise gate's sidechain detection circuit. You can choose profiles such as Low-Pass, High-Pass, Band-Pass, or Band-Reject to determine exactly which frequency characteristics of the incoming audio will trigger the gate.

ae_data.ch.N.gatesc.f.manualText: Establishes the primary centerpoint frequency for the gate's sidechain filter network. Adjusting this value ensures that the gate opens only when specific instrument frequencies (such as the fundamental punch of a kick drum) pass through the sidechain detection filter.

ae_data.ch.N.gatesc.q.manualText: Adjusts the Quality Factor (Q) or sharpness of the gate sidechain filter band. A higher value creates a narrow, selective frequency window to isolate a single specific element, while a lower value broadens the filter response to trigger the gate from a wider range of neighboring frequencies.

ae_data.ch.N.gatesc.src.manualText: Selects the specific input channel or internal bus that acts as the trigger source for the gate's sidechain logic. This allows you to route an external signal (such as using a kick drum track) to automatically key or control the gating behavior of this channel.

ae_data.ch.N.gatesc.tap.manualText: Determines the precise location within the source channel's signal path from which the sidechain audio feed is captured. Options typically include pre-EQ, post-EQ, or post-fader positions, altering how processed or dynamic the sidechain trigger signal will be.

ae_data.ch.N.eq.on.manualText: This parameter indicates whether the equalizer (EQ) for this path is active. When enabled, the EQ settings for this channel will be applied to the audio signal, allowing you to shape the tonal balance of the monitor mix. The EQ can be used to boost or cut specific frequency ranges, helping performers to better hear certain elements in the mix or to reduce unwanted frequencies that may cause feedback or muddiness.

ae_data.ch.N.eq.mdl.manualText: Specifies the software emulation model loaded into the main channel equalizer slot. This parameter allows you to select between different tonal processing styles, including modern transparent digital EQs, British console emulations, or vintage American proportional-Q hardware designs.

ae_data.ch.N.eq.mix.labelText: Dry/Wet Parallel Signal Effect Blending Percentage
ae_data.ch.N.eq.mix.manualText: Controls the balance between the original un-equalized signal (dry) and the equalized signal (wet). This allows for parallel equalization, letting you dial in drastic curves or aggressive tonal shifts while blending back raw transients to maintain a more natural instrument character.

ae_data.ch.N.eq.lg.manualText: Adjusts the fixed gain level for the low-frequency equalization band. Modifying this value allows you to boost or cut the bass region of the audio spectrum, adding warmth and weight to an instrument or reducing low-end clutter to clean up the mix.

ae_data.ch.N.eq.lf.manualText: Sets the corner or center frequency for the low-equalization band. This target frequency defines the exact boundary in the lower register where the low band's gain changes will be centered or begin to roll off.

ae_data.ch.N.eq.lq.manualText: Controls the Quality Factor (Q) or bandwidth response for the low-frequency equalizer band. This setting determines how wide or narrow the frequency bell curve is around the low centerpoint, governing how much sub-bass or low-mid content is affected by gain adjustments.

ae_data.ch.N.eq.leq.manualText: Selects the filter shape or geometry mode for the low-equalization band. You can toggle this setting between a shelf filter curve (which affects all frequencies below the corner point equally) and a parametric bell curve (which targets a localized frequency zone).

ae_data.ch.N.eq.1g.manualText: The gain control for the first parametric EQ band, which allows you to adjust the amount of boost or cut applied to the selected frequency range. This parameter can be used to shape the tonal balance of the monitor mix, helping performers to better hear certain elements or to reduce unwanted frequencies.

ae_data.ch.N.eq.1f.manualText: The frequency control for the first parametric EQ band, which allows you to adjust the center frequency of the selected frequency range. This parameter can be used to shape the tonal balance of the monitor mix, helping performers to better hear certain elements or to reduce unwanted frequencies.

ae_data.ch.N.eq.1q.manualText: The Q-factor control for the first parametric EQ band, which allows you to adjust the bandwidth of the selected frequency range. A higher Q-factor results in a narrower bandwidth, while a lower Q-factor results in a wider bandwidth. This parameter can be used to fine-tune the tonal balance of the monitor mix.

ae_data.ch.N.eq.2g.manualText: The gain control for the second parametric EQ band, which allows you to adjust the amount of boost or cut applied to the selected frequency range. ae_data.ch.N.eq.hg.manualText: Adjusts the fixed gain level for the high-frequency equalization band. Modifying this value allows you to boost or cut the treble region of the audio spectrum, adding brightness, clarity, and air to an instrument or reducing harshness and high-frequency noise.

ae_data.ch.N.eq.hf.manualText: Sets the corner or center frequency for the high-equalization band. This target frequency defines the exact boundary in the upper register where the high band's gain changes will be centered or begin to lift.

ae_data.ch.N.eq.hq.manualText: Controls the Quality Factor (Q) or bandwidth response for the high-frequency equalizer band. This setting determines how wide or narrow the frequency bell curve is around the high centerpoint, governing how much upper-mid or extreme high-end content is affected.

ae_data.ch.N.eq.heq.manualText: Selects the filter shape or geometry mode for the high-equalization band. You can toggle this setting between a shelf filter curve (which affects all frequencies above the corner point equally) and a parametric bell curve (which targets a localized frequency zone).

ae_data.ch.N.dyn.on.manualText: Activates or deactivates the main dynamics processor (compressor/limiter) module for this channel. Turning this switch on engages the configured dynamic processing settings to control signal peaks, while turning it off completely bypasses the module.

ae_data.ch.N.dyn.mdl.manualText: Specifies the software emulation model loaded into the channel's dynamics processing slot. This allows you to choose between various compression styles, such as clean digital, vintage optical, VCA, or classic FET hardware emulations.

ae_data.ch.N.dyn.mix.labelText: Dry/Wet Parallel Signal Effect Blending Percentage
ae_data.ch.N.dyn.mix.manualText: Controls the blend percentage between the dry (uncompressed) and wet (compressed) audio signals. This parameter enables parallel compression, allowing you to heavily squash the signal for punch and sustain while blending back the uncompressed audio to preserve natural transient dynamics.

ae_data.ch.N.dyn.gain.manualText: Adjusts the clean makeup gain level applied at the output stage of the dynamics module. This parameter is used to compensate for the overall volume reduction caused by compression, allowing you to bring the average level of the processed audio back up to match the rest of the mix.

ae_data.ch.N.dyn.thr.manualText: Sets the threshold level for the channel's compressor. Audio signal peaks that cross above this designated decibel threshold will trigger the gain reduction process, determining exactly when the compressor starts working to restrict dynamic range.

ae_data.ch.N.dyn.ratio.labelText: Dynamics Core Compression Reduction Ratio Multiplier
ae_data.ch.N.dyn.ratio.manualText: Determines the ratio multiplier used for gain reduction once the audio signal exceeds the compressor threshold. For example, a 4:1 ratio means that for every 4 dB the input signal goes over the threshold, the output level will only increase by 1 dB.

ae_data.ch.N.dyn.knee.labelText: Compression Knee Curve Softness Transition Depth
ae_data.ch.N.dyn.knee.manualText: Adjusts the sharpness or softness of the compression turn-on curve around the threshold point. A hard knee introduces compression immediately as the signal crosses the threshold, while a soft knee creates a gradual, more transparent transition as gain reduction begins.

ae_data.ch.N.dyn.det.manualText: Selects the methodology used by the sidechain circuit to analyze the signal amplitude envelope. You can switch between Peak mode (reacts instantly to brief transient voltage spikes) and RMS mode (averages the signal energy over time for a smoother, more human-like response).

ae_data.ch.N.dyn.att.labelText: Dynamics Envelope Reaction Attack Time Constants
ae_data.ch.N.dyn.att.manualText: Sets the attack time constant, which determines how quickly the compressor applies full gain reduction after the input signal crosses above the threshold. Fast attack times catch brief peaks quickly, while slower attack times let initial musical transients pass through untouched.

ae_data.ch.N.dyn.hld.labelText: Dynamics Processing Envelope Peak Hold Duration
ae_data.ch.N.dyn.hld.manualText: Defines the specific hold duration during which the compressor maintains its peak gain reduction status before entering the release phase. This temporary freeze prevents the compressor from modulating or pumping rapidly when handling sustained low-frequency wave cycles.

ae_data.ch.N.dyn.rel.labelText: Dynamics Envelope Recovery Release Time Constants
ae_data.ch.N.dyn.rel.manualText: Sets the release time constant, which determines how quickly the compressor stops applying gain reduction and returns to unity level after the input signal drops back below the designated threshold. Fast release times restore normal volume rapidly, while slower times provide smooth, transparent leveling.

ae_data.ch.N.dyn.env.labelText: Dynamics Gain Processing Expansion Envelope Curve Model
ae_data.ch.N.dyn.env.manualText: Selects the specific mathematical curve model for the dynamics processor's gain expansion envelope. This parameter modifies how smoothly or aggressively the downward expansion algorithms track the decay of an audio signal, tailoring the gate/expander reaction to different sound sources.

ae_data.ch.N.dyn.auto.manualText: Toggles the automatic timing optimization engine for the compressor. When activated, this circuit dynamically evaluates the incoming signal characteristics to automatically adapt the attack, release, and internal thresholds, optimizing response in real time for highly variable audio signals.

ae_data.ch.N.dynxo.depth.manualText: Determines the maximum amount of signal attenuation applied when the crossover expander or gate module is fully closed. Also known as the floor range, a lower depth setting creates a subtle attenuation of background noise, while a maximum depth completely silences the signal path.

ae_data.ch.N.dynxo.type.manualText: Selects the filter profile type utilized within the crossover dynamic processor. You can choose profiles such as Low-Pass, High-Pass, Band-Pass, or Band-Reject to isolate specific frequency zones for band-limited expansion or gating.

ae_data.ch.N.dynxo.f.manualText: Establishes the primary centerpoint or split frequency for the crossover dynamics module. Adjusting this value determines the exact boundary where the signal is divided, isolating targeted frequency content for independent dynamic compression or expansion.

ae_data.ch.N.dynxo.q.manualText: Adjusts the Quality Factor (Q) or sharpness of the crossover filter band. A higher value creates a narrow, selective frequency window to isolate a single specific element, while a lower value broadens the filter response to encompass neighboring frequencies.

ae_data.ch.N.dynsc.type.manualText: Selects the filter profile type utilized within the compressor's sidechain detection circuit. You can choose profiles such as Low-Pass, High-Pass, Band-Pass, or Band-Reject to determine exactly which frequency characteristics of the incoming audio will trigger the compressor.

ae_data.ch.N.dynsc.f.manualText: Establishes the primary centerpoint frequency for the compressor's sidechain filter network. Adjusting this value ensures that the compressor reacts only when specific instrument frequencies (such as low-end plosives on a vocal microphone) pass through the sidechain filter.

ae_data.ch.N.dynsc.q.manualText: Adjusts the Quality Factor (Q) or sharpness of the compressor sidechain filter band. A higher value creates a narrow, selective frequency window to isolate a specific resonant frequency, while a lower value broadens the filter response to trigger compression from a wider range of tones.

ae_data.ch.N.dynsc.src.manualText: Selects the specific input channel or internal bus that acts as the trigger source for the compressor's sidechain logic. This allows you to route an external signal (such as using a bass guitar track) to automatically key or control the compression behavior of this channel.

ae_data.ch.N.dynsc.tap.manualText: Determines the precise location within the source channel's signal path from which the sidechain audio feed is captured. Options typically include pre-EQ, post-EQ, or post-fader positions, altering how processed or dynamic the sidechain trigger signal will be.

ae_data.ch.N.preins.on.manualText: Activates or deactivates the pre-processing insert stage for the channel. Toggling this switch to the active position engages the assigned external loop or internal effect rack slot, while turning it off completely bypasses the insertion loop.

ae_data.ch.N.preins.ins.labelText: External Hardware FX Loop / Internal Rack Insert Slot
ae_data.ch.N.preins.ins.manualText: Specifies the physical external hardware FX loop or internal software virtual rack slot routed to this pre-processing position. This parameter allows you to patch outboard analog outboard gear or digital system effects directly into the channel signal path.

ae_data.ch.N.main.N.on.manualText: Activates or deactivates the signal routing path from this channel to the targeted main output bus. Enabling this parameter sends the channel mix to the master outputs, while disabling it disconnects the path, muting the channel specifically within that master mix.

ae_data.ch.N.main.N.lvl.manualText: Controls the absolute send level or volume configuration for the signal being routed to the designated master output bus. Adjusting this parameter shifts the balance of the channel within the primary stereo or multi-channel main mix.

ae_data.ch.N.main.N.pre.manualText: Toggles the routing location of the main bus injection point within the channel strip. Engaging this switch changes the routing to capture a pre-equalizer or pre-dynamics signal, sending the clean, raw audio to the main mix before it undergoes any channel EQ or dynamic processing modifications.

ae_data.ch.N.send.N.on.manualText: Activates or deactivates the signal routing path from this channel to the designated auxiliary send bus. Enabling this switch allows the channel's audio signal to flow into the auxiliary mix, while disabling it completely breaks the connection to mute this specific channel send.

ae_data.ch.N.send.N.lvl.manualText: Controls the individual send volume or signal level directed from this channel to the assigned auxiliary send bus. Adjusting this parameter determines the balance of this specific channel within that particular auxiliary mix, such as a stage monitor feed or an effects loop.

ae_data.ch.N.send.N.pon.labelText: Insert Node Return Loop Processing Switch
ae_data.ch.N.send.N.pon.manualText: Toggles the operational state of the processing return loop for the assigned insert node on this send path. Enabling this switch patches the returned processed audio signal back into the active auxiliary send stream, while disabling it bypasses the return loop entirely.

ae_data.ch.N.send.N.mode.manualText: Configures the specialized solo mode behavior and operational routing rules for this send bus path. This setting determines how the send bus responds to global console solo commands, controlling whether it is muted, isolated, or prioritized during solo-in-place operations.

ae_data.ch.N.send.N.plink.labelText: Parallel Stereo Processing Core Link Link Offset
ae_data.ch.N.send.N.plink.manualText: Sets the link alignment offset value for coordinated parallel stereo core processing across linked send paths. This parameter ensures accurate phase tracking and level calibration symmetry between the left and right channels when running dual-bus processing configurations.

ae_data.ch.N.send.N.pan.manualText: The pan control for the channel auxiliary send path, which allows you to adjust the stereo positioning of the signal sent to a stereo aux bus pair. Moving the pan control left or right shifts the spatial balance of the channel signal within that specific auxiliary monitor or effect mix.

ae_data.ch.N.send.MX1.on.manualText: Activates or deactivates the specific routing path from this channel to the Matrix 1 (MX1) mix bus. Turning this switch to the active position routes the channel's audio signal into the first matrix mixer block, while turning it off completely silences the feed to Matrix 1.

ae_data.ch.N.send.MX1.lvl.manualText: Adjusts the specific send volume or audio signal level routed from this channel into the Matrix 1 (MX1) mixer input stage. Modifying this level alters how prominently this channel's audio is blended into the independent Matrix 1 zone mix.

ae_data.ch.N.send.MX1.pon.labelText: Insert Node Return Loop Processing Switch
ae_data.ch.N.send.MX1.pon.manualText: Toggles the operational status of the processing return loop for the insert node on the Matrix 1 (MX1) send path. Activating this parameter injects the processed external loop return signal back into the active Matrix 1 mix path.

ae_data.ch.N.send.MX1.mode.manualText: Determines the specialized solo behavior rules applied to the Matrix 1 (MX1) send circuit. This sets whether the Matrix 1 feed remains safely active (Solo Safe) or automatically deactivates when other channels on the control surface are isolated via solo commands.

ae_data.ch.N.send.MX1.plink.labelText: Parallel Stereo Processing Core Link Link Offset
ae_data.ch.N.send.MX1.plink.manualText: Defines the parallel stereo processing link tracking offset configuration specifically assigned to the Matrix 1 (MX1) send node. This maintains proper stereo image coherence and parameter symmetry when routing to linked multi-channel matrix output zones.

ae_data.ch.N.send.MX1.pan.manualText: Controls the independent stereo pan balance of this channel's feed when directed to a stereo-linked Matrix 1 (MX1) zone bus. This parameter lets you position the audio element anywhere from left to right within the physical sound field of the first matrix output mix.
