ae_data.ch.N.send.MX8.on.manualText: Activates or deactivates the specific routing path from this channel to the Matrix 8 (MX8) mix bus. Turning this switch to the active position routes the channel's audio signal into the eighth matrix mixer block, while turning it off completely silences the feed to Matrix 8.

ae_data.ch.N.send.MX8.lvl.manualText: Adjusts the specific send volume or audio signal level routed from this channel into the Matrix 8 (MX8) mixer input stage. Modifying this level alters how prominently this channel's audio is blended into the independent Matrix 8 zone mix.

ae_data.ch.N.send.MX8.pon.labelText: Insert Node Return Loop Processing Switch
ae_data.ch.N.send.MX8.pon.manualText: Toggles the operational status of the processing return loop for the insert node on the Matrix 8 (MX8) send path. Activating this parameter injects the processed external loop return signal back into the active Matrix 8 mix path.

ae_data.ch.N.send.MX8.mode.manualText: Determines the specialized solo behavior rules applied to the Matrix 8 (MX8) send circuit. This sets whether the Matrix 8 feed remains safely active (Solo Safe) or automatically deactivates when other channels on the control surface are isolated via solo commands.

ae_data.ch.N.send.MX8.plink.labelText: Parallel Stereo Processing Core Link Link Offset
ae_data.ch.N.send.MX8.plink.manualText: Defines the parallel stereo processing link tracking offset configuration specifically assigned to the Matrix 8 (MX8) send node. This maintains proper stereo image coherence and parameter symmetry when routing to linked multi-channel matrix output zones.

ae_data.ch.N.send.MX8.pan.manualText: Controls the independent stereo pan balance of this channel's feed when directed to a stereo-linked Matrix 8 (MX8) zone bus. This parameter lets you position the audio element anywhere from left to right within the physical sound field of the eighth matrix output mix.

ae_data.ch.N.tapwid.labelText: Bus Tap Stereo Spacing Width Output Scale
ae_data.ch.N.tapwid.manualText: Controls the output scale modifier for the stereo spacing width applied at the bus tap node. Adjusting this value scales the spatial separation depth of the stereo field for signal components branched off to internal auxiliary processing chains or downstream summing networks.

ae_data.ch.N.postins.on.manualText: Activates or deactivates the post-processing insert stage for the channel. Toggling this switch to the active position engages the assigned external loop or internal virtual effect rack slot after the primary channel processing blocks, while turning it off completely bypasses the post-insert loop.

ae_data.ch.N.postins.mode.manualText: Configures the specialized solo mode behavior and operational routing rules for the post-processing insert path. This setting determines how the insert loop behaves during global console solo commands, controlling whether the external or virtual effect returns are muted or isolated.

ae_data.ch.N.postins.ins.labelText: External Hardware FX Loop / Internal Rack Insert Slot
ae_data.ch.N.postins.ins.manualText: Specifies the physical external hardware FX loop or internal software virtual rack slot routed to this post-processing position. This parameter allows you to patch outboard analog processing equipment or digital system effects directly after the channel fader and main EQ/dynamics.

ae_data.ch.N.postins.w.labelText: Spatial Stereo Field Expansion Enhancer Width
ae_data.ch.N.postins.w.manualText: Adjusts the width parameter for the spatial stereo field expansion enhancer embedded within the post-insert processing stage. Increasing this value widens the side-channel information to create a broad, cinematic acoustic space, while decreasing it collapses the signal toward a focused center point.

ae_data.ch.N.tags.manualText: Stores custom metadata strings or searchable categorization tags for the channel. This allows system engineers and operators to label, group, filter, or instantly recall specific channel blocks across the console surface or layout manager based on venue, instrument family, or layout logic.

ae_data.ch.N.gate.range.labelText: FX Envelope Dynamic Sweep Processing Range Depth
ae_data.ch.N.gate.range.manualText: Sets the maximum boundary range or depth limit for the noise gate's dynamic filter sweep or attenuation curve. This dictates how heavily the filter envelope modulates or suppresses low-level signal elements when the gate threshold is not met, establishing the processing floor.

ae_data.ch.N.gate.att.labelText: Dynamics Envelope Reaction Attack Time Constants
ae_data.ch.N.gate.att.manualText: Sets the attack time constant for the noise gate, determining how rapidly the gate transitions from an attenuated state to unity gain once the incoming audio signal crosses above the established threshold. Fast settings open the gate instantly to capture sudden transients cleanly.

ae_data.ch.N.gate.hld.labelText: Dynamics Processing Envelope Peak Hold Duration
ae_data.ch.N.gate.hld.manualText: Defines the exact hold duration for which the noise gate remains fully open after the audio signal drops back below the designated threshold. This brief hold prevents the gate from chattering, stuttering, or closing prematurely during momentary pauses in speech or musical notes.

ae_data.ch.N.gate.rel.labelText: Dynamics Envelope Recovery Release Time Constants
ae_data.ch.N.gate.rel.manualText: Sets the release time constant for the noise gate, controlling how gradually or rapidly the processor applies attenuation after the hold duration expires. A longer release provides a natural, smooth fade-out for trailing instrument decays, while a shorter release abruptly shuts out ambient bleed.

ae_data.ch.N.gate.acc.labelText: FX Processor Internal Parameter Accumulator Constant
ae_data.ch.N.gate.acc.manualText: Controls the internal feedback accumulator constant within the effects processor's sidechain tracking loop. This parameter fine-tunes how the detection algorithm weights and averages past signal values, modifying the envelope tracking smoothness for highly dynamic or complex material.

ae_data.ch.N.gate.ratio.labelText: Dynamics Core Compression Reduction Ratio Multiplier
ae_data.ch.N.gate.ratio.manualText: Sets the attenuation ratio multiplier applied by the gate module when operating in expansion mode. Adjusting this value determines how aggressively the signal below the threshold is reduced relative to its original input level, scaling from a subtle downward expander to a hard noise gate.

ae_data.ch.N.dyn.ingain.labelText: FX Return Path Processing Stage Input Gain Attenuation
ae_data.ch.N.dyn.ingain.manualText: Adjusts the input gain attenuation applied at the entry stage of the effects return dynamics processor. This allows you to scale and optimize the incoming hot signal level before it reaches the compression core, ensuring adequate headroom and preventing internal processor overloading.

ae_data.ch.N.dyn.peak.manualText: Configures the peak ceiling detection threshold percentage for the internal brickwall limiter on the dynamics module. This parameter dictates the absolute safety boundary, forcing instant level clamping if a heavy signal transient threatens to introduce unwanted digital distortion or clipping.

ae_data.ch.N.dyn.mode.manualText: Configures the solo mode behavior and operational routing rules for the dynamics block. This parameter sets how the processor handles signal states during global console solo actions, ensuring that active dynamic sidechains or linked paths stay intact when tracks are isolated.

ae_data.aux.N.in.set.srcauto.manualText: Configures the automatic input source selection behavior for the auxiliary channel. When enabled, this feature allows the system to automatically switch between primary and backup auxiliary hardware paths based on signal presence or specific error conditions, maintaining continuous audio flow.

ae_data.aux.N.in.set.altsrc.manualText: Defines the secondary or backup alternate input source assigned to this auxiliary channel. This alternate path serves as a redundant failover option that the system can quickly switch to if the primary auxiliary input connection encounters a signal dropout or hardware fault.

ae_data.aux.N.in.set.inv.manualText: Toggles the phase (polarity) inversion status of the auxiliary input signal. Engaging phase inversion flips the audio waveform 180 degrees, which is critical for correcting acoustic phase cancellation issues when combining this auxiliary signal with other source paths or submixes.

ae_data.aux.N.in.set.trim.manualText: Adjusts the digital trim gain or attenuation level applied directly to the incoming auxiliary signal. This parameter allows you to fine-tune and balance input levels across different auxiliary channels before the signal hits the main gain stages, mixing bus, or effects rack.

ae_data.aux.N.in.set.bal.manualText: Controls the stereo balance and physical width positioning of a stereo auxiliary source within the soundstage. Adjusting this parameter shifts the relative level between the left and right channels or alters the stereo field width, helping to place the auxiliary return precisely in the mix.

ae_data.aux.N.in.set.dlymode.manualText: Sets the preferred measurement unit used to calculate and display the auxiliary channel delay. You can toggle this mode between units such as milliseconds (ms), meters (m), feet (ft), or samples, allowing for intuitive adjustments depending on your phase alignment requirements.

ae_data.aux.N.in.set.dly.manualText: Determines the exact amount of time delay applied to the auxiliary channel's input signal. This parameter is used for precise time alignment, ensuring that auxiliary audio feeds arrive at the mixing bus in perfect sync with the rest of the console channels to avoid comb filtering.

ae_data.aux.N.in.set.dlyon.manualText: Enables or disables the delay processing stage for the auxiliary channel. Toggling this parameter to the active state applies the configured time alignment delay value to the audio path, while turning it off completely bypasses the delay processing block.

ae_data.aux.N.in.conn.grp.manualText: Assigns the auxiliary channel to a specific control or link group. When designated to a link group, specific parameters like fader levels, mutes, or processing settings can be adjusted simultaneously across all grouped auxiliary channels for simplified mixing workflow.

ae_data.aux.N.in.conn.in.manualText: Specifies the physical or digital hardware routing path for the local microphone preamplifier assigned to this auxiliary channel. This parameter allows you to patch a specific hardware input jack to the internal virtual routing structure.

ae_data.aux.N.in.conn.altgrp.manualText: Designates the auxiliary channel to an alternative safe group configuration, such as a Mute Safe or VCA Safe group. This ensures that when global system commands or scene recalls are executed, the parameters of this auxiliary channel remain unaffected.

ae_data.aux.N.in.conn.altin.manualText: Determines the specific routing index or hardware address for an alternative preamplifier input channel. This parameter allows the system to reference a secondary hardware input patch, making it easy to hot-swap auxiliary input signals.

ae_data.aux.N.clink.manualText: Sets the status flag for linking adjacent auxiliary channels into a coordinated stereo pair. When enabled, internal DSP parameters such as dynamics filters, EQ configurations, and gain settings are linked together, maintaining identical stereo processing symmetry.

ae_data.aux.N.col.labelText: Console Strip LCD Backlight Color Index
ae_data.aux.N.col.manualText: Determines the specific color index used for the physical console strip's LCD backlight display on this auxiliary track. This parameter allows you to color-code auxiliary channels for quick visual identification on the hardware surface.

ae_data.aux.N.name.manualText: Stores the custom text string used to name or label the auxiliary channel on the console scribblestrip and digital user interface. This parameter replaces generic aux numbers with recognizable names for specific mixes, monitor feeds, or effects.

ae_data.aux.N.icon.manualText: Selects the visual icon index code displayed on the auxiliary channel's LCD screen. This parameter allows you to assign graphical symbols (such as headphones or wedge monitors) to the console strip, providing immediate visual confirmation of the track type.

ae_data.aux.N.led.labelText: Physical Control Surface LED Accent Ring Switch
ae_data.aux.N.led.manualText: Controls the operational state of the physical LED accent ring surrounding the auxiliary channel encoder on the hardware control surface. This switch toggles the LED indicator behavior between standard parameter tracking or custom highlighting.

ae_data.aux.N.mute.manualText: Engages the absolute mute override function for the auxiliary channel. Activating this parameter instantly cuts the audio signal path at the designated mute stage, silencing the auxiliary output without altering the underlying fader or gain positions.

ae_data.aux.N.fdr.manualText: Represents the exact volume or attenuation position value of the physical motorized fader on the auxiliary control surface. Adjusting this parameter updates the output level of the auxiliary bus and moves the physical fader to match.

ae_data.aux.N.pan.manualText: The pan control for the auxiliary channel path, which allows you to adjust the stereo positioning of the audio signal. By moving the pan control left or right, you can create a sense of space and separation in the main mix or destination stereo stem.

ae_data.aux.N.wid.manualText: Adjusts the perceived width of the stereo field for a stereo-linked auxiliary channel. Modifying this control expands the stereo separation outward for a broader soundstage, or narrows it down toward a focused center point to tighten spatial positioning.

ae_data.aux.N.solosafe.manualText: Activates Solo Safe mode for this auxiliary channel. When enabled, this track is isolated from the Solo-In-Place system, meaning it will not be automatically muted when other console channels are soloed. This is vital for maintaining effects returns or master submix integrity.

ae_data.aux.N.mon.manualText: Sets the destination or target bus for the auxiliary channel's monitor path routing. This parameter dictates where the auxiliary mix signal is sent, allowing you to route specific audio feeds directly to performer headphones, stage wedges, or control room monitors.

ae_data.aux.N.eq.on.manualText: This parameter indicates whether the equalizer (EQ) for this path is active. When enabled, the EQ settings for this channel will be applied to the audio signal, allowing you to shape the tonal balance of the monitor mix. The EQ can be used to boost or cut specific frequency ranges, helping performers to better hear certain elements in the mix or to reduce unwanted frequencies that may cause feedback or muddiness.

ae_data.aux.N.eq.mdl.manualText: Specifies the software emulation model loaded into the main auxiliary equalizer slot. This parameter allows you to select between different tonal processing styles, including modern transparent digital EQs, British console emulations, or vintage hardware designs.

ae_data.aux.N.eq.mix.labelText: Dry/Wet Parallel Signal Effect Blending Percentage
ae_data.aux.N.eq.mix.manualText: Controls the balance between the original un-equalized auxiliary signal (dry) and the equalized signal (wet). This allows for parallel equalization, letting you dial in drastic curves or aggressive tonal shifts while blending back raw transients to maintain a more natural character.

ae_data.aux.N.eq.lg.manualText: Adjusts the fixed gain level for the low-frequency equalization band on the auxiliary path. Modifying this value allows you to boost or cut the bass region of the audio spectrum, adding warmth and weight to the mix or reducing low-end clutter.

ae_data.aux.N.eq.lf.manualText: Sets the corner or center frequency for the auxiliary low-equalization band. This target frequency defines the exact boundary in the lower register where the low band's gain changes will be centered or begin to roll off.

ae_data.aux.N.eq.lq.manualText: Controls the Quality Factor (Q) or bandwidth response for the auxiliary low-frequency equalizer band. This setting determines how wide or narrow the frequency bell curve is around the low centerpoint, governing how much sub-bass or low-mid content is affected by gain adjustments.

ae_data.aux.N.eq.leq.manualText: Selects the filter shape or geometry mode for the auxiliary low-equalization band. You can toggle this setting between a shelf filter curve (which affects all frequencies below the corner point equally) and a parametric bell curve (which targets a localized frequency zone).

ae_data.aux.N.eq.1g.manualText: The gain control for the first parametric EQ band, which allows you to adjust the amount of boost or cut applied to the selected frequency range. This parameter can be used to shape the tonal balance of the monitor mix, helping performers to better hear certain elements or to reduce unwanted frequencies.

ae_data.aux.N.eq.1f.manualText: The frequency control for the first parametric EQ band, which allows you to adjust the center frequency of the selected frequency range. This parameter can be used to shape the tonal balance of the monitor mix, helping performers to better hear certain elements or to reduce unwanted frequencies.

ae_data.aux.N.eq.1q.manualText: The Q-factor control for the first parametric EQ band, which allows you to adjust the bandwidth of the selected frequency range. A higher Q-factor results in a narrower bandwidth, while a lower Q-factor results in a wider bandwidth. This parameter can be used to fine-tune the tonal balance of the monitor mix.

ae_data.aux.N.eq.2g.manualText: The gain control for the second parametric EQ band, which allows you to adjust the amount of boost or cut applied to the selected frequency range. This parameter can be used to shape the tonal balance of the monitor mix, helping performers to better hear certain elements or to reduce unwanted frequencies.

ae_data.aux.N.eq.2f.manualText: The frequency control for the second parametric EQ band, which allows you to adjust the center frequency of the selected frequency range. This parameter can be used to shape the tonal balance of the monitor mix, helping performers to better hear certain elements or to reduce unwanted frequencies.

ae_data.aux.N.eq.2q.manualText: The Q-factor control for the second parametric EQ band, which allows you to adjust the bandwidth of the selected frequency range. A higher Q-factor results in a narrower bandwidth, while a lower Q-factor results in a wider bandwidth. This parameter can be used to fine-tune the tonal balance of the monitor mix.

ae_data.aux.N.eq.3g.manualText: The gain control for the third parametric EQ band, which allows you to adjust the amount of boost or cut applied to the selected frequency range. This parameter can be used to shape the tonal balance of the monitor mix, helping performers to better hear certain elements or to reduce unwanted frequencies.

ae_data.aux.N.eq.3f.manualText: The frequency control for the third parametric EQ band, which allows you to adjust the center frequency of the selected frequency range. This parameter can be used to shape the tonal balance of the monitor mix, helping performers to better hear certain elements or to reduce unwanted frequencies.

ae_data.aux.N.eq.3q.manualText: The Q-factor control for the third parametric EQ band, which allows you to adjust the bandwidth of the selected frequency range. A higher Q-factor results in a narrower bandwidth, while a lower Q-factor results in a wider bandwidth. This parameter can be used to fine-tune the tonal balance of the monitor mix.

ae_data.aux.N.eq.4g.manualText: The gain control for the fourth parametric EQ band, which allows you to adjust the amount of boost or cut applied to the selected frequency range. This parameter can be used to shape the tonal balance of the monitor mix, helping performers to better hear certain elements or to reduce unwanted frequencies.

ae_data.aux.N.eq.4f.manualText: The frequency control for the fourth parametric EQ band, which allows you to adjust the center frequency of the selected frequency range. This parameter can be used to shape the tonal balance of the monitor mix, helping performers to better hear certain elements or to reduce unwanted frequencies.

ae_data.aux.N.eq.4q.manualText: The Q-factor control for the fourth parametric EQ band, which allows you to adjust the bandwidth of the selected frequency range. A higher Q-factor results in a narrower bandwidth, while a lower Q-factor results in a wider bandwidth. This parameter can be used to fine-tune the tonal balance of the monitor mix.

ae_data.aux.N.eq.hg.manualText: Adjusts the fixed gain level for the high-frequency equalization band on the auxiliary path. Modifying this value allows you to boost or cut the treble region of the audio spectrum, adding brightness, clarity, and air to the mix or reducing harshness and high-frequency noise.

ae_data.aux.N.eq.hf.manualText: Sets the corner or center frequency for the auxiliary high-equalization band. This target frequency defines the exact boundary in the upper register where the high band's gain changes will be centered or begin to lift.

ae_data.aux.N.eq.hq.manualText: Controls the Quality Factor (Q) or bandwidth response for the auxiliary high-frequency equalizer band. This setting determines how wide or narrow the frequency bell curve is around the high centerpoint, governing how much upper-mid or extreme high-end content is affected.

ae_data.aux.N.eq.heq.manualText: Selects the filter shape or geometry mode for the auxiliary high-equalization band. You can toggle this setting between a shelf filter curve (which affects all frequencies above the corner point equally) and a parametric bell curve (which targets a localized frequency zone).

ae_data.aux.N.dyn.on.manualText: Activates or deactivates the main dynamics processor (compressor/limiter) module for this auxiliary channel. Turning this switch on engages the configured dynamic processing settings to control submix or effect signal peaks, while turning it off completely bypasses the module.

ae_data.aux.N.dyn.mdl.manualText: Specifies the software emulation model loaded into the auxiliary channel's dynamics processing slot. This allows you to choose between various compression styles, such as clean digital, vintage optical, VCA, or classic FET hardware emulations adapted for bus processing.

ae_data.aux.N.dyn.mix.labelText: Dry/Wet Parallel Signal Effect Blending Percentage
ae_data.aux.N.dyn.mix.manualText: Controls the blend percentage between the dry (uncompressed) and wet (compressed) audio signals on the auxiliary path. This parameter enables parallel compression, allowing you to heavily squash the bus signal for punch and sustain while blending back the uncompressed audio to preserve natural transients.

ae_data.aux.N.dyn.gain.manualText: Adjusts the clean makeup gain level applied at the output stage of the auxiliary dynamics module. This parameter is used to compensate for the overall volume reduction caused by compression, allowing you to bring the average level of the processed bus audio back up to match the rest of the mix.

ae_data.aux.N.dyn.thr.manualText: Sets the threshold level for the auxiliary channel's compressor. Audio signal peaks that cross above this designated decibel threshold will trigger the gain reduction process, determining exactly when the compressor starts working to restrict the dynamic range of the bus.

ae_data.aux.N.dyn.range.labelText: FX Envelope Dynamic Sweep Processing Range Depth
ae_data.aux.N.dyn.range.manualText: Sets the maximum boundary range or depth limit for the dynamic filter sweep or attenuation curve within the auxiliary processor. This dictates how heavily the envelope modulates or suppresses low-level signal elements when the threshold conditions are not met.

ae_data.aux.N.dyn.att.labelText: Dynamics Envelope Reaction Attack Time Constants
ae_data.aux.N.dyn.att.manualText: Sets the attack time constant, which determines how quickly the auxiliary compressor applies full gain reduction after the input signal crosses above the threshold. Fast attack times catch brief peaks quickly, while slower attack times let initial musical transients pass through the bus untouched.

ae_data.aux.N.dyn.hld.labelText: Dynamics Processing Envelope Peak Hold Duration
ae_data.aux.N.dyn.hld.manualText: Defines the specific hold duration during which the auxiliary compressor maintains its peak gain reduction status before entering the release phase. This temporary freeze prevents the compressor from modulating or pumping rapidly when handling sustained low-frequency wave cycles on the bus.

ae_data.aux.N.dyn.rel.labelText: Dynamics Envelope Recovery Release Time Constants
ae_data.aux.N.dyn.rel.manualText: Sets the release time constant, which determines how quickly the auxiliary compressor stops applying gain reduction and returns to unity level after the input signal drops back below the designated threshold. Fast release times restore normal volume rapidly, while slower times provide smooth, transparent leveling.

ae_data.aux.N.dyn.acc.labelText: FX Processor Internal Parameter Accumulator Constant
ae_data.aux.N.dyn.acc.manualText: Controls the internal feedback accumulator constant within the auxiliary processor's tracking loop. This parameter fine-tunes how the detection algorithm weights and averages past signal values, modifying the envelope tracking smoothness for highly dynamic or complex material on the bus.

ae_data.aux.N.dyn.ratio.labelText: Dynamics Core Compression Reduction Ratio Multiplier
ae_data.aux.N.dyn.ratio.manualText: Determines the ratio multiplier used for gain reduction once the auxiliary bus signal exceeds the compressor threshold. For example, a 4:1 ratio means that for every 4 dB the input signal goes over the threshold, the output level will only increase by 1 dB.

ae_data.aux.N.dynsc.type.manualText: Selects the filter profile type utilized within the auxiliary compressor's sidechain detection circuit. You can choose profiles such as Low-Pass, High-Pass, Band-Pass, or Band-Reject to determine exactly which frequency characteristics of the incoming audio will trigger the compressor.

ae_data.aux.N.dynsc.f.manualText: Establishes the primary centerpoint frequency for the auxiliary compressor's sidechain filter network. Adjusting this value ensures that the compressor reacts only when specific instrument frequencies (such as problematic mid-range build-up) pass through the sidechain filter.

ae_data.aux.N.dynsc.q.manualText: Adjusts the Quality Factor (Q) or sharpness of the auxiliary compressor's sidechain filter band. A higher value creates a narrow, selective frequency window to isolate a specific resonant frequency build-up, while a lower value broadens the filter response to trigger compression from a wider range of tones.

ae_data.aux.N.dynsc.src.manualText: Selects the specific input channel or internal bus that acts as the trigger source for the auxiliary compressor's sidechain logic. This allows you to route an external signal to automatically key or control the compression behavior of this auxiliary path.

ae_data.aux.N.dynsc.tap.manualText: Determines the precise location within the source channel's signal path from which the sidechain audio feed is captured for the auxiliary compressor. Options typically include pre-EQ, post-EQ, or post-fader positions, altering how processed or dynamic the sidechain trigger signal will be.

ae_data.aux.N.preins.on.manualText: Activates or deactivates the pre-processing insert stage for the auxiliary channel. Toggling this switch to the active position engages the assigned external loop or internal effect rack slot, while turning it off completely bypasses the insertion loop.

ae_data.aux.N.preins.ins.labelText: External Hardware FX Loop / Internal Rack Insert Slot
ae_data.aux.N.preins.ins.manualText: Specifies the physical external hardware FX loop or internal software virtual rack slot routed to this pre-processing position on the auxiliary channel. This parameter allows you to patch outboard analog outboard gear or digital system effects directly into the signal path.

ae_data.aux.N.main.N.on.manualText: Activates or deactivates the signal routing path from this auxiliary channel to the targeted main output bus. Enabling this parameter sends the auxiliary mix to the master outputs, while disabling it disconnects the path, muting the channel specifically within that master mix.

ae_data.aux.N.main.N.lvl.manualText: Controls the absolute send level or volume configuration for the auxiliary signal being routed to the designated master output bus. Adjusting this parameter shifts the balance of the auxiliary channel within the primary stereo or multi-channel main mix.

ae_data.aux.N.main.N.pre.manualText: Toggles the routing location of the main bus injection point within the auxiliary channel strip. Engaging this switch changes the routing to capture a pre-equalizer or pre-dynamics signal, sending the clean, raw audio to the main mix before it undergoes any channel EQ or dynamic processing modifications.

ae_data.aux.N.send.N.on.manualText: Activates or deactivates the signal routing path from this auxiliary channel to the designated auxiliary send bus. Enabling this switch allows the track's audio signal to flow into the destination auxiliary mix, while disabling it completely breaks the connection to mute this specific send.

ae_data.aux.N.send.N.lvl.manualText: Controls the individual send volume or signal level directed from this auxiliary channel to the assigned destination auxiliary send bus. Adjusting this parameter determines the balance of this specific track within that particular destination auxiliary mix.

ae_data.aux.N.send.N.pon.labelText: Insert Node Return Loop Processing Switch
ae_data.aux.N.send.N.pon.manualText: Toggles the operational state of the processing return loop for the assigned insert node on this auxiliary send path. Enabling this switch patches the returned processed audio signal back into the active send stream, while disabling it bypasses the return loop entirely.

ae_data.aux.N.send.N.mode.manualText: Configures the specialized solo mode behavior and operational routing rules for this auxiliary send path. This setting determines how the send path responds to global console solo commands, controlling whether it is muted, isolated, or prioritized during solo-in-place operations.

ae_data.aux.N.send.N.plink.labelText: Parallel Stereo Processing Core Link Link Offset
ae_data.aux.N.send.N.plink.manualText: Sets the link alignment offset value for coordinated parallel stereo core processing across linked auxiliary send paths. This parameter ensures accurate phase tracking and level calibration symmetry between the left and right channels when running dual-bus processing configurations.

ae_data.aux.N.send.N.pan.manualText: The pan control for the auxiliary channel send path, which allows you to adjust the stereo positioning of the signal sent to a destination stereo bus pair. Moving the pan control left or right shifts the spatial balance of the signal within that specific monitor or effect mix.

ae_data.aux.N.send.MX1.on.manualText: Activates or deactivates the specific routing path from this auxiliary channel to the Matrix 1 (MX1) mix bus. Turning this switch to the active position routes the signal into the first matrix mixer block, while turning it off completely silences the feed to Matrix 1.

ae_data.aux.N.send.MX1.lvl.manualText: Adjusts the specific send volume or audio signal level routed from this auxiliary channel into the Matrix 1 (MX1) mixer input stage. Modifying this level alters how prominently this track's audio is blended into the independent Matrix 1 zone mix.

ae_data.aux.N.send.MX1.pon.labelText: Insert Node Return Loop Processing Switch
ae_data.aux.N.send.MX1.pon.manualText: Toggles the operational status of the processing return loop for the insert node on the Matrix 1 (MX1) auxiliary send path. Activating this parameter injects the processed external loop return signal back into the active Matrix 1 mix path.

ae_data.aux.N.send.MX1.mode.manualText: Determines the specialized solo behavior rules applied to the Matrix 1 (MX1) auxiliary send circuit. This sets whether the Matrix 1 feed remains safely active (Solo Safe) or automatically deactivates when other channels on the control surface are isolated via solo commands.

ae_data.aux.N.send.MX1.plink.labelText: Parallel Stereo Processing Core Link Link Offset
ae_data.aux.N.send.MX1.plink.manualText: Defines the parallel stereo processing link tracking offset configuration specifically assigned to the Matrix 1 (MX1) auxiliary send node. This maintains proper stereo image coherence and parameter symmetry when routing to linked multi-channel matrix output zones.

ae_data.aux.N.send.MX1.pan.manualText: Controls the independent stereo pan balance of this auxiliary channel's feed when directed to a stereo-linked Matrix 1 (MX1) zone bus. This parameter lets you position the audio element anywhere from left to right within the physical sound field of the first matrix output mix.

ae_data.aux.N.send.MX2.on.manualText: Activates or deactivates the specific routing path from this auxiliary channel to the Matrix 2 (MX2) mix bus. Turning this switch to the active position routes the signal into the second matrix mixer block, while turning it off completely silences the feed to Matrix 2.

ae_data.aux.N.send.MX2.lvl.manualText: Adjusts the specific send volume or audio signal level routed from this auxiliary channel into the Matrix 2 (MX2) mixer input stage. Modifying this level alters how prominently this track's audio is blended into the independent Matrix 2 zone mix.

ae_data.aux.N.send.MX2.pon.labelText: Insert Node Return Loop Processing Switch
ae_data.aux.N.send.MX2.pon.manualText: Toggles the operational status of the processing return loop for the insert node on the Matrix 2 (MX2) auxiliary send path. Activating this parameter injects the processed external loop return signal back into the active Matrix 2 mix path.

ae_data.aux.N.send.MX2.mode.manualText: Determines the specialized solo behavior rules applied to the Matrix 2 (MX2) auxiliary send circuit. This sets whether the Matrix 2 feed remains safely active (Solo Safe) or automatically deactivates when other channels on the control surface are isolated via solo commands.

ae_data.aux.N.send.MX2.plink.labelText: Parallel Stereo Processing Core Link Link Offset

ae_data.aux.N.tags.manualText: Stores custom metadata strings or searchable categorization tags for the auxiliary channel. This allows system engineers and operators to label, group, filter, or instantly recall specific auxiliary blocks across the console surface or layout manager based on mix type or layout logic.

ae_data.bus.N.in.set.inv.manualText: Toggles the phase (polarity) inversion status of the main bus input path. Engaging phase inversion flips the audio waveform 180 degrees, which is crucial for correcting acoustic or electronic phase cancellation issues when combining multiple summing groups or parent buses.

ae_data.bus.N.in.set.trim.manualText: Adjusts the digital trim gain or attenuation level applied directly to the incoming bus signal path. This parameter allows you to fine-tune and balance total gain structuring across different mix buses before the summing stream hits processing inserts or main output stages.

ae_data.bus.N.in.set.bal.manualText: Controls the stereo balance and physical width positioning of the audio data flowing through this mix bus. Adjusting this parameter shifts the relative balance between the left and right summing channels, letting you orient the bus image accurately across the main soundstage.

ae_data.bus.N.col.labelText: Console Strip LCD Backlight Color Index
ae_data.bus.N.col.manualText: Determines the specific color index used for the physical console strip's LCD backlight display on this mix bus strip. This parameter allows you to color-code buses (e.g., drum subgroups vs. instrument stems) for instant visual identification on the control surface.

ae_data.bus.N.name.manualText: Stores the custom text string used to name or label the mix bus on the console scribblestrip and digital user interface. This parameter replaces generic bus numbers with clear, user-defined terms like 'Drums', 'Vocals', or 'Main FX'.

ae_data.bus.N.icon.manualText: Selects the visual icon index code displayed on the bus channel's LCD screen. This parameter allows you to assign graphical symbols to the console strip, providing immediate visual confirmation of the bus type or group contents.

ae_data.bus.N.led.labelText: Physical Control Surface LED Accent Ring Switch
ae_data.bus.N.led.manualText: Controls the operational state of the physical LED accent ring surrounding the mix bus encoder on the hardware control surface. This switch toggles the LED indicator behavior between standard parameter tracking or custom highlighting modes.

ae_data.bus.N.busmono.labelText: Global Bus Center-Sum Mono Downmix Rule Switch
ae_data.bus.N.busmono.manualText: Toggles the center-sum mono downmix rule configuration for this bus. When activated, this switch collapses a stereo or multi-channel bus configuration down into a uniform monaural signal path using equal center-sum level coefficients, ensuring absolute phase alignment.

ae_data.bus.N.mute.manualText: Engages the absolute mute override function for the mix bus path. Activating this parameter instantly cuts the audio signal path at the designated master summing output stage, silencing the entire bus without altering individual channel sends or internal processor structures.

ae_data.bus.N.fdr.manualText: Represents the exact master volume or attenuation position value of the physical motorized fader on the mix bus control surface. Adjusting this parameter scales the global volume output level of the summing bus and moves the physical hardware fader to match.

ae_data.bus.N.pan.manualText: The master pan control for the mix bus path, which allows you to adjust the stereo positioning of the entire combined bus signal. By moving the pan control left or right, you can alter the spatial placement of this entire submix subgroup within the wider master framework.

ae_data.bus.N.wid.manualText: Adjusts the master perceived width of the stereo field for the mix bus channel. Modifying this control expands the stereo separation outward for a broader soundstage across the whole bus, or narrows it down toward a focused center point to tighten the subgroup's spatial imaging.

ae_data.bus.N.mon.manualText: Sets the destination or target bus for the mix bus channel's monitor path routing. This parameter dictates where the combined bus signal is directed, allowing you to route specific master submixes directly to performer headphones, stage wedges, or control room monitors.

ae_data.bus.N.eq.on.manualText: This parameter indicates whether the equalizer (EQ) for this path is active. When enabled, the EQ settings for this bus will be applied to the audio signal, allowing you to shape the tonal balance of the monitor mix. The EQ can be used to boost or cut specific frequency ranges, helping performers to better hear certain elements in the mix or to reduce unwanted frequencies that may cause feedback or muddiness.

ae_data.bus.N.eq.mdl.manualText: Specifies the software emulation model loaded into the mix bus equalizer slot. This parameter allows you to select between different tonal processing styles for your global submix, including modern transparent digital EQs, classic British bus EQs, or vintage hardware console emulations.

ae_data.bus.N.eq.mix.labelText: Dry/Wet Parallel Signal Effect Blending Percentage
ae_data.bus.N.eq.mix.manualText: Controls the balance between the original un-equalized bus signal (dry) and the equalized signal (wet). This allows for parallel equalization across the entire mix bus, letting you apply broad tonal shifts while maintaining the original transient power and dynamics of the combined tracks.

ae_data.bus.N.eq.lg.manualText: Adjusts the fixed gain level for the low-frequency equalization band on the mix bus path. Modifying this value allows you to boost or cut the baseline response of the entire submix, adding structural warmth and weight or carving out unnecessary low-end mud across grouped instruments.

ae_data.bus.N.eq.lf.manualText: Sets the corner or center frequency for the mix bus low-equalization band. This target frequency defines the exact boundary in the lower register where the low band's global gain changes will be centered or begin to roll off.

ae_data.bus.N.eq.lq.manualText: Controls the Quality Factor (Q) or bandwidth response for the mix bus low-frequency equalizer band. This setting determines how wide or narrow the frequency bell curve is around the low centerpoint, governing how much sub-bass or low-mid content is affected across the entire bus.

ae_data.bus.N.eq.leq.manualText: Selects the filter shape or geometry mode for the mix bus low-equalization band. You can toggle this setting between a shelf filter curve (which affects all frequencies below the corner point equally) and a parametric bell curve (which targets a localized frequency zone).

ae_data.bus.N.eq.1g.manualText: The gain control for the first parametric EQ band, which allows you to adjust the amount of boost or cut applied to the selected frequency range. This parameter can be used to shape the tonal balance of the monitor mix, helping performers to better hear certain elements or to reduce unwanted frequencies.

ae_data.bus.N.eq.1f.manualText: The frequency control for the first parametric EQ band, which allows you to adjust the center frequency of the selected frequency range. This parameter can be used to shape the tonal balance of the monitor mix, helping performers to better hear certain elements or to reduce unwanted frequencies.

ae_data.bus.N.eq.1q.manualText: The Q-factor control for the first parametric EQ band, which allows you to adjust the bandwidth of the selected frequency range. A higher Q-factor results in a narrower bandwidth, while a lower Q-factor results in a wider bandwidth. This parameter can be used to fine-tune the tonal balance of the monitor mix.

ae_data.bus.N.eq.hg.manualText: Adjusts the fixed gain level for the high-frequency equalization band on the mix bus. Modifying this value allows you to boost or cut the treble region of the entire submix, adding general air, sheen, and top-end clarity, or softening collective high-frequency harshness.

ae_data.bus.N.eq.hf.manualText: Sets the corner or center frequency for the mix bus high-equalization band. This target frequency defines the exact boundary in the upper register where the high band's global gain adjustments will be concentrated or begin to lift.

ae_data.bus.N.eq.hq.manualText: Controls the Quality Factor (Q) or bandwidth response for the mix bus high-frequency equalizer band. This setting determines how wide or narrow the frequency bell curve is around the high centerpoint, governing how much upper-mid or extreme high-end content is altered across the bus.

ae_data.bus.N.eq.heq.manualText: Selects the filter shape or geometry mode for the mix bus high-equalization band. You can toggle this setting between a shelf filter curve (which affects all frequencies above the corner point equally) and a parametric bell curve (which targets a localized frequency zone).

ae_data.bus.N.eq.tilt.labelText: Tilt EQ Spectrum Balance Tone Shifter
ae_data.bus.N.eq.tilt.manualText: Adjusts the Tilt EQ parameter for the global mix bus, acting as a spectrum balance tone shifter around a central pivot frequency. Boosting this value brightens the entire bus by raising high frequencies while cutting lows, whereas reducing it warms up the submix by tilting down the highs and boosting the bass.

ae_data.bus.N.dyn.on.manualText: Activates or deactivates the main dynamics processor (compressor/limiter) module for this mix bus. Turning this switch on engages the configured dynamic processing settings to glue, smooth, or restrict the dynamic peaks of the summed audio tracks, while turning it off completely bypasses the block.

ae_data.bus.N.dyn.mdl.manualText: Specifies the software emulation model loaded into the mix bus dynamics processing slot. This allows you to choose between various compression styles optimized for submix gluing, such as clean digital, vintage VCA bus compressors, optical levelers, or classic vari-mu designs.

ae_data.bus.N.dyn.mix.labelText: Dry/Wet Parallel Signal Effect Blending Percentage
ae_data.bus.N.dyn.mix.manualText: Controls the blend percentage between the uncompressed bus signal (dry) and the compressed bus signal (wet). This parameter enables parallel bus compression, allowing you to heavily compress the subgroup for dense punch and sustain while blending back the raw track transients for natural dynamics.

ae_data.bus.N.dyn.gain.manualText: Adjusts the clean makeup gain level applied at the output stage of the mix bus dynamics module. This parameter is used to compensate for the overall volume reduction caused by bus compression, allowing you to restore or normalize the gain structure of the summed mix block.

ae_data.bus.N.dyn.thr.manualText: Sets the threshold level for the mix bus compressor core. Combined audio signal peaks that cross above this designated decibel threshold will trigger the gain reduction process, determining exactly at what point the bus compressor begins attenuating and gluing the mix.

ae_data.bus.N.dyn.ratio.labelText: Dynamics Core Compression Reduction Ratio Multiplier
ae_data.bus.N.dyn.ratio.manualText: Determines the ratio multiplier used for gain reduction once the combined mix bus signal exceeds the compressor threshold. For bus compression, lower ratios like 1.5:1 or 2:1 are typically used for gentle gluing, whereas higher ratios provide aggressive peak control.

ae_data.bus.N.dyn.knee.labelText: Compression Knee Curve Softness Transition Depth
ae_data.bus.N.dyn.knee.manualText: Adjusts the sharpness or softness of the compression turn-on curve around the mix bus threshold point. A soft knee creates a gradual, more transparent transition as gain reduction begins, which is highly desirable for keeping submix leveling musical and unobtrusive.

ae_data.bus.N.dyn.det.manualText: Selects the methodology used by the sidechain circuit to analyze the combined bus signal amplitude. Switching between Peak mode (reacts instantly to explosive transients) and RMS mode (averages signal energy over time) alters whether the bus compressor behaves as a limiter or a smooth leveler.

ae_data.bus.N.dyn.att.labelText: Dynamics Envelope Reaction Attack Time Constants
ae_data.bus.N.dyn.att.manualText: Sets the attack time constant, which determines how quickly the mix bus compressor applies full gain reduction after the summed signal crosses above the threshold. Slower attack times are preferred on buses to allow the snap of drum transients to pass through cleanly before compression hits.

ae_data.bus.N.dyn.hld.labelText: Dynamics Processing Envelope Peak Hold Duration
ae_data.bus.N.dyn.hld.manualText: Defines the specific hold duration during which the mix bus compressor maintains its peak gain reduction status before entering the release phase. This temporary freeze prevents the compressor from modulating or pumping rapidly when handling sustained low-frequency wave cycles or dense bass transients across the summed audio path.

ae_data.bus.N.dyn.rel.labelText: Dynamics Envelope Recovery Release Time Constants
ae_data.bus.N.dyn.rel.manualText: Sets the release time constant, which determines how quickly the mix bus compressor stops applying gain reduction and returns to unity level after the summed signal drops back below the designated threshold. Careful adjustment of this recovery curve is crucial on a master bus to achieve transparent gluing without introducing pumping artifacts.

ae_data.bus.N.dyn.env.labelText: Dynamics Gain Processing Expansion Envelope Curve Model
ae_data.bus.N.dyn.env.manualText: Selects the specific mathematical curve model for the dynamics processor's gain expansion envelope on the mix bus. This parameter modifies how smoothly or aggressively the downward expansion algorithms track the collective signal decay, shaping how the bus gating or expansion logic handles ambient noise bleed.

ae_data.bus.N.dyn.auto.manualText: Toggles the automatic timing optimization engine for the mix bus compressor. When activated, this circuit dynamically evaluates the complex, multi-source material inside the submix to automatically adapt the attack, release, and internal thresholds, optimizing response in real time for highly variable summing signals.

ae_data.bus.N.dynxo.depth.manualText: Determines the maximum amount of signal attenuation applied when the crossover expander or gate module on the mix bus is fully closed. Also known as the floor range, a lower depth setting creates a subtle attenuation of submix background noise, while a maximum depth completely silences the crossover path.

ae_data.bus.N.dynxo.type.manualText: Selects the filter profile type utilized within the mix bus crossover dynamic processor. You can choose profiles such as Low-Pass, High-Pass, Band-Pass, or Band-Reject to isolate specific frequency zones of your submix for band-limited expansion or gating processing.

ae_data.bus.N.dynxo.f.manualText: Establishes the primary centerpoint or split frequency for the mix bus crossover dynamics module. Adjusting this value determines the exact boundary where the submix signal is divided, isolating targeted frequency content for independent dynamic compression or expansion rules.

ae_data.bus.N.dynxo.q.manualText: Adjusts the Quality Factor (Q) or sharpness of the mix bus crossover filter band. A higher value creates a narrow, selective frequency window to isolate a single specific resonant band within the submix, while a lower value broadens the filter response to encompass neighboring frequencies.

ae_data.bus.N.dynsc.type.manualText: Selects the filter profile type utilized within the mix bus compressor's sidechain detection circuit. You can choose profiles such as Low-Pass, High-Pass, Band-Pass, or Band-Reject to determine exactly which frequency characteristics of the incoming audio will trigger the bus compressor.

ae_data.bus.N.dynsc.f.manualText: Establishes the primary centerpoint frequency for the mix bus compressor's sidechain filter network. Adjusting this value ensures that the compressor reacts only when specific instrument frequencies (such as low-end mud or vocal plosives in the combined mix) pass through the sidechain filter.

ae_data.bus.N.dynsc.q.manualText: Adjusts the Quality Factor (Q) or sharpness of the mix bus compressor sidechain filter band. A higher value creates a narrow, selective frequency window to isolate a specific resonant frequency build-up, while a lower value broadens the filter response to trigger compression from a wider range of tones.

ae_data.bus.N.dynsc.src.manualText: Selects the specific input channel or internal bus that acts as the trigger source for the mix bus compressor's sidechain logic. This allows you to route an external signal to automatically key or control the compression behavior of this summed mix path.

ae_data.bus.N.dynsc.tap.manualText: Determines the precise location within the source channel's signal path from which the sidechain audio feed is captured for the mix bus compressor. Options typically include pre-EQ, post-EQ, or post-fader positions, altering how processed or dynamic the sidechain trigger signal will be.

ae_data.bus.N.preins.on.manualText: Activates or deactivates the pre-processing insert stage for the mix bus. Toggling this switch to the active position engages the assigned external loop or internal effect rack slot before the primary bus processing blocks, while turning it off completely bypasses the insertion loop.

ae_data.bus.N.preins.ins.labelText: External Hardware FX Loop / Internal Rack Insert Slot
ae_data.bus.N.preins.ins.manualText: Specifies the physical external hardware FX loop or internal software virtual rack slot routed to this pre-processing position on the mix bus channel. This parameter allows you to patch outboard analog outboard gear or digital system effects directly into the signal path.

ae_data.bus.N.main.N.on.manualText: Activates or deactivates the signal routing path from this mix bus to the targeted main output bus. Enabling this parameter sends the combined bus submix to the master outputs, while disabling it disconnects the path, muting the bus specifically within that master mix.

ae_data.bus.N.main.N.lvl.manualText: Controls the absolute send level or volume configuration for the mix bus signal being routed to the designated master output bus. Adjusting this parameter shifts the balance of this submix within the primary stereo or multi-channel main output mix.

ae_data.bus.N.main.N.pre.manualText: Toggles the routing location of the main bus injection point within the mix bus strip. Engaging this switch changes the routing to capture a pre-equalizer or pre-dynamics signal, sending the clean, raw audio to the main mix before it undergoes any bus EQ or dynamic processing modifications.

ae_data.bus.N.send.N.on.manualText: Activates or deactivates the signal routing path from this mix bus to the designated auxiliary send destination. Enabling this switch allows the combined bus signal to flow into the auxiliary mix, while disabling it completely breaks the connection to mute this specific bus send.

ae_data.bus.N.send.N.lvl.manualText: Controls the individual send volume or signal level directed from this mix bus to the assigned auxiliary send destination. Adjusting this parameter determines the balance of this entire submix subgroup within that particular auxiliary monitor or effect feed.

ae_data.bus.N.send.N.pre.manualText: Toggles the routing location of the auxiliary send injection point within the mix bus strip. Engaging this switch changes the routing to capture a pre-equalizer or pre-dynamics signal, routing the submix to the auxiliary path before it undergoes any internal bus EQ or dynamic processing modifications.

ae_data.bus.N.send.MX1.on.manualText: Activates or deactivates the specific routing path from this mix bus to the Matrix 1 (MX1) mix bus. Turning this switch to the active position routes the combined bus signal into the first matrix mixer block, while turning it off completely silences the feed to Matrix 1.

ae_data.bus.N.send.MX1.lvl.manualText: Adjusts the specific send volume or audio signal level routed from this mix bus into the Matrix 1 (MX1) mixer input stage. Modifying this level alters how prominently this submix group is blended into the independent Matrix 1 zone mix.

ae_data.bus.N.send.MX1.pre.manualText: Toggles the routing location of the Matrix 1 (MX1) send injection point within the mix bus strip. ae_data.bus.N.postins.ins.labelText: External Hardware FX Loop / Internal Rack Insert Slot
ae_data.bus.N.postins.ins.manualText: Specifies the physical external hardware FX loop or internal software virtual rack slot routed to this post-processing position on the mix bus. This parameter allows you to patch outboard analog outboard gear or digital system mastering effects directly into the summed bus path after main processing.

ae_data.bus.N.dly.on.manualText: Enables or disables the delay processing stage for the mix bus path. Toggling this parameter to the active state applies the configured time alignment delay value to the audio path, while turning it off completely bypasses the delay processing block to eliminate path latency.

ae_data.bus.N.dly.mode.manualText: Configures the operational solo mode behavior and routing priority specifically for the mix bus delay module sidechain. This setting ensures that time-aligned paths or look-ahead detection windows behave correctly when other sections of the console are isolated.

ae_data.bus.N.dly.dly.manualText: Determines the exact amount of time delay applied to the mix bus output path. This parameter is typically used for master speaker time alignment, aligning secondary zone delays, or compensating for spatial transmission timing gaps in large venue PA setups.

ae_data.bus.N.tags.manualText: Stores custom metadata strings or searchable categorization tags for the mix bus. This allows system engineers and operators to label, group, filter, or instantly recall specific mix buses across the console surface or layout manager based on master routing logic.

ae_data.main.N.in.set.inv.manualText: Toggles the phase (polarity) inversion status of the main master output bus. Engaging phase inversion flips the audio waveform 180 degrees, which serves as a global corrective measure for system-wide wiring phase issues or acoustic cancellation across the main PA.

ae_data.main.N.in.set.trim.manualText: Adjusts the digital trim gain or attenuation level applied directly at the entry stage of the main master bus. This allows you to scale the ultimate summing input signal before it feeds into final master EQ, bus limiting, or physical output matrices.

ae_data.main.N.in.set.bal.manualText: Controls the balance and physical width positioning of the global stereo field on the main master output. Adjusting this parameter corrects left/right shifts or balances the primary stereo soundstage across the venue's left and right main speaker towers.

ae_data.main.N.col.labelText: Console Strip LCD Backlight Color Index
ae_data.main.N.col.manualText: Determines the specific color index used for the physical console strip's LCD backlight display on the main master fader. This allows you to color-code the primary stereo or surround master strips so they stand out distinctly from channel and subgroup rows.

ae_data.main.N.name.manualText: Stores the custom text string used to name or label the main master output bus on the physical scribblestrip and user interface. This parameter replaces generic master numbering with clear identifiers like 'Main L/R', 'Center Sub', or 'Broadcast Master'.

ae_data.main.N.icon.manualText: Selects the visual icon index code displayed on the main master fader's LCD screen. This parameter applies specific master-tier graphical symbols to the console strip, providing immediate visual confirmation of primary system outputs.

ae_data.main.N.led.labelText: Physical Control Surface LED Accent Ring Switch
ae_data.main.N.led.manualText: Controls the operational state of the physical LED accent ring surrounding the main master fader rotary encoder. This switch toggles the LED encoder ring behavior between global system parameter tracking or absolute visual highlighting.

ae_data.main.N.busmono.labelText: Global Bus Center-Sum Mono Downmix Rule Switch
ae_data.main.N.busmono.manualText: Toggles the center-sum mono downmix rule configuration for the main master bus. When activated, this switch collapses the entire master stereo field down into a uniform monaural signal path using equal center-sum level coefficients, ideal for mono venue testing.

ae_data.main.N.mute.manualText: Engages the absolute master mute override function for the entire main output bus. Activating this parameter instantly cuts the final audio signal path, completely silencing the console's primary outputs to protect amplifiers and speakers without altering fader coordinates.

ae_data.main.N.fdr.manualText: Represents the exact volume or attenuation position value of the main master motorized fader on the control surface. Adjusting this parameter updates the absolute level of the total audio mix passing out of the main mixing core to your speaker systems.

ae_data.main.N.pan.manualText: The master pan control for the main output bus, which allows you to adjust the global spatial positioning of the final mix. By moving the pan control left or right, you can offset the entire spatial image balance across your main stereo sound system.

ae_data.main.N.wid.manualText: Adjusts the master perceived width of the stereo field for the main master output. Modifying this control expands the full mix outward for a wider, more dramatic soundstage, or narrows it down toward a focused center point to check mono compatibility.

ae_data.main.N.mon.manualText: Sets the destination or target bus for the main master channel's monitor path routing. This parameter dictates where the global mix signal is duplicated or tapped, allowing you to route copy feeds directly to headphones, engineering wedges, or local control rooms.

ae_data.main.N.eq.on.manualText: This parameter indicates whether the equalizer (EQ) for this path is active. When enabled, the EQ settings for this main will be applied to the audio signal, allowing you to shape the tonal balance of the monitor mix. The EQ can be used to boost or cut specific frequency ranges, helping performers to better hear certain elements in the mix or to reduce unwanted frequencies that may cause feedback or muddiness.

ae_data.main.N.eq.mdl.manualText: Specifies the software emulation model loaded into the main master bus equalizer slot. This parameter allows you to select between different tonal processing styles for your global master output, including clean transparent digital mastering EQs or classic analog console stereo bus emulations.

ae_data.main.N.eq.mix.labelText: Dry/Wet Parallel Signal Effect Blending Percentage
ae_data.main.N.eq.mix.manualText: Controls the balance between the original un-equalized master signal (dry) and the equalized master signal (wet). This allows for parallel equalization across the final master mix, letting you dial in broad sweetening curves while blending back raw transients to maintain original dynamic impact.

ae_data.main.N.eq.lg.manualText: Adjusts the fixed gain level for the low-frequency equalization band on the main master output. Modifying this value allows you to boost or cut the global bass response of the entire mix, adding anchoring weight and warmth or tightening sub-bass clutter across the complete acoustic spectrum.

ae_data.main.N.eq.lf.manualText: Sets the corner or center frequency for the main master low-equalization band. This target frequency defines the exact boundary in the lower register where the final master EQ's low-end gain adjustments will be centered or begin to roll off.

ae_data.main.N.eq.lq.manualText: Controls the Quality Factor (Q) or bandwidth response for the main master low-frequency equalizer band. This setting determines how wide or narrow the frequency bell curve is around the master low centerpoint, governing how much global sub-bass or low-mid content is affected.

ae_data.main.N.eq.leq.manualText: Selects the filter shape or geometry mode for the main master low-equalization band. You can toggle this setting between a shelf filter curve (which affects all low frequencies below the corner point equally) and a parametric bell curve (which targets a localized, specific bass frequency zone).

ae_data.main.N.eq.1g.manualText: The gain control for the first parametric EQ band, which allows you to adjust the amount of boost or cut applied to the selected frequency range. This parameter can be used to shape the tonal balance of the monitor mix, helping performers to better hear certain elements or to reduce unwanted frequencies.

ae_data.main.N.eq.1f.manualText: The frequency control for the first parametric EQ band, which allows you to adjust the center frequency of the selected frequency range. This parameter can be used to shape the tonal balance of the monitor mix, helping performers to better hear certain elements or to reduce unwanted frequencies.

ae_data.main.N.eq.1q.manualText: The Q-factor control for the first parametric EQ band, which allows you to adjust the bandwidth of the selected frequency range. A higher Q-factor results in a narrower bandwidth, while a lower Q-factor results in a wider bandwidth. This parameter can be used to fine-tune the tonal balance of the monitor mix.

ae_data.main.N.eq.hg.manualText: Adjusts the fixed gain level for the high-frequency equalization band on the main master output. Modifying this value allows you to boost or cut the global treble region of the entire final mix, adding top-end air, presence, and master clarity, or softening collective high-frequency harshness.

ae_data.main.N.eq.hf.manualText: Sets the corner or center frequency for the main master high-equalization band. This target frequency defines the exact boundary in the upper register where the final master EQ's high-frequency gain adjustments will be concentrated or begin to lift.

ae_data.main.N.eq.hq.manualText: Controls the Quality Factor (Q) or bandwidth response for the main master high-frequency equalizer band. This setting determines how wide or narrow the frequency bell curve is around the master high centerpoint, governing how much global upper-mid or extreme high-end content is altered.

ae_data.main.N.eq.heq.manualText: Selects the filter shape or geometry mode for the main master high-equalization band. You can toggle this setting between a shelf filter curve (which affects all high frequencies above the corner point equally) and a parametric bell curve (which targets a localized, specific treble frequency zone).

ae_data.main.N.eq.tilt.labelText: Tilt EQ Spectrum Balance Tone Shifter
ae_data.main.N.eq.tilt.manualText: Adjusts the Tilt EQ parameter for the global main master output, acting as a spectrum balance tone shifter around a central pivot frequency. Boosting this value brightens the final mix by raising high frequencies while cutting lows, whereas reducing it warms up the overall output by tilting down the highs and boosting the bass.

ae_data.main.N.dyn.on.manualText: Activates or deactivates the main dynamics processor module on the primary master output bus. Turning this switch on engages the configured dynamic processing settings to glue, smooth, or restrict the dynamic peaks of the total audio mix, while turning it off completely bypasses the block.

ae_data.main.N.dyn.mdl.manualText: Specifies the software emulation model loaded into the main master dynamics processing slot. This allows you to choose between various compression and limiting styles optimized for master gluing, such as transparent digital mastering limiters, vintage VCA stereo bus compressors, or classic vari-mu designs.

ae_data.main.N.dyn.mix.labelText: Dry/Wet Parallel Signal Effect Blending Percentage
ae_data.main.N.dyn.mix.manualText: Controls the blend percentage between the uncompressed signal (dry) and the compressed signal (wet) on the primary master output path. This parameter enables parallel master compression, allowing you to heavily squash the final mix for dense punch and energy while blending back the raw transients for natural dynamics.

ae_data.main.N.dyn.gain.manualText: Adjusts the clean makeup gain level applied at the output stage of the main master dynamics module. This parameter is used to compensate for the overall volume reduction caused by master compression, allowing you to restore, optimize, or normalize the absolute gain structure of your total output stream.

ae_data.main.N.dyn.thr.manualText: Sets the threshold level for the main master fader's compressor core. Global audio signal peaks that cross above this designated decibel threshold will trigger the gain reduction process, determining exactly at what point the master compressor begins attenuating and gluing the final mix.

ae_data.main.N.dyn.ratio.labelText: Dynamics Core Compression Reduction Ratio Multiplier
ae_data.main.N.dyn.ratio.manualText: Determines the ratio multiplier used for gain reduction once the global master signal exceeds the compressor threshold. For master compression, lower ratios like 1.5:1 or 2:1 are typically used for gentle gluing, whereas higher ratios or infinity settings convert the module into a brickwall safety limiter.

ae_data.main.N.dyn.knee.labelText: Compression Knee Curve Softness Transition Depth
ae_data.main.N.dyn.knee.manualText: Adjusts the sharpness or softness of the compression turn-on curve around the main master threshold point. A soft knee creates a gradual, more transparent transition as gain reduction begins, which is highly desirable for keeping master leveling musical, smooth, and completely transparent.

ae_data.main.N.dyn.det.manualText: Selects the methodology used by the sidechain circuit to analyze the final master signal amplitude. Switching between Peak mode (reacts instantly to explosive transients to protect hardware speakers) and RMS mode (averages signal energy over time) alters whether the master compressor behaves as a limiter or a smooth leveler.

ae_data.main.N.dyn.att.labelText: Dynamics Envelope Reaction Attack Time Constants
ae_data.main.N.dyn.att.manualText: Sets the attack time constant, which determines how quickly the master compressor applies full gain reduction after the total signal crosses above the threshold. Slower attack times are preferred on the main output to allow the snap of musical transients to pass through cleanly before compression hits.

ae_data.main.N.dyn.hld.labelText: Dynamics Processing Envelope Peak Hold Duration
ae_data.main.N.dyn.hld.manualText: Defines the specific hold duration during which the main master compressor maintains its peak gain reduction status before entering the release phase. This temporary freeze prevents the compressor from modulating or pumping rapidly when handling sustained low-frequency wave cycles or dense bass transients across the final output path.

ae_data.main.N.dyn.rel.labelText: Dynamics Envelope Recovery Release Time Constants
ae_data.main.N.dyn.rel.manualText: Sets the release time constant, which determines how quickly the master compressor stops applying gain reduction and returns to unity level after the global signal drops back below the designated threshold. Careful adjustment of this recovery curve is crucial on the main fader to achieve transparent gluing without introducing pumping artifacts.

ae_data.main.N.dyn.env.labelText: Dynamics Gain Processing Expansion Envelope Curve Model
ae_data.main.N.dyn.env.manualText: Selects the specific mathematical curve model for the dynamics processor's gain expansion envelope on the master path. This parameter modifies how smoothly or aggressively the downward expansion algorithms track the collective signal decay, shaping how master gating or expansion logic handles ambient venue noise.

ae_data.main.N.dyn.auto.manualText: Toggles the automatic timing optimization engine for the main master compressor. When activated, this circuit dynamically evaluates the complex, multi-layered material inside the final mix to automatically adapt the attack, release, and internal thresholds, optimizing response in real time for highly variable summing signals.

ae_data.main.N.dynxo.depth.manualText: Determines the maximum amount of signal attenuation applied when the crossover expander or gate module on the master bus is fully closed. Also known as the floor range, a lower depth setting creates a subtle attenuation of master background noise, while a maximum depth completely silences the crossover path.

ae_data.main.N.dynxo.type.manualText: Selects the filter profile type utilized within the main master crossover dynamic processor. You can choose profiles such as Low-Pass, High-Pass, Band-Pass, or Band-Reject to isolate specific frequency zones of your final mix for band-limited expansion or gating processing.

ae_data.main.N.dynxo.f.manualText: Establishes the primary centerpoint or split frequency for the master bus crossover dynamics module. Adjusting this value determines the exact boundary where the full mix signal is divided, isolating targeted frequency content for independent dynamic compression or expansion rules.

ae_data.main.N.dynxo.q.manualText: Adjusts the Quality Factor (Q) or sharpness of the main master crossover filter band. A higher value creates a narrow, selective frequency window to isolate a single specific resonant band within the full mix, while a lower value broadens the filter response to encompass neighboring frequencies.

ae_data.main.N.dynsc.type.manualText: Selects the filter profile type utilized within the main master compressor's sidechain detection circuit. You can choose profiles such as Low-Pass, High-Pass, Band-Pass, or Band-Reject to determine exactly which frequency characteristics of the incoming audio will trigger the master compressor.

ae_data.main.N.dynsc.f.manualText: Establishes the primary centerpoint frequency for the master compressor's sidechain filter network. Adjusting this value ensures that the compressor reacts only when specific instrument frequencies (such as low-end boominess or harsh upper-mid buildups in the total mix) pass through the sidechain filter.

ae_data.main.N.dynsc.q.manualText: Adjusts the Quality Factor (Q) or sharpness of the master compressor sidechain filter band. A higher value creates a narrow, selective frequency window to isolate a specific resonant frequency buildup, while a lower value broadens the filter response to trigger compression from a wider range of tones.

ae_data.main.N.dynsc.src.manualText: Selects the specific input channel or internal bus that acts as the trigger source for the main master compressor's sidechain logic. This allows you to route an external signal (such as an independent timecode or reference path) to automatically key or control the compression behavior of the final mix.

ae_data.main.N.dynsc.tap.manualText: Determines the precise location within the source channel's signal path from which the sidechain audio feed is captured for the main master compressor. Options typically include pre-EQ, post-EQ, or post-fader positions, altering how processed or dynamic the sidechain trigger signal will be.

ae_data.main.N.preins.on.manualText: Activates or deactivates the pre-processing insert stage for the main master output. Toggling this switch to the active position engages the assigned external loop or internal effect rack slot before the primary master processing blocks, while turning it off completely bypasses the insertion loop.

ae_data.main.N.preins.ins.labelText: External Hardware FX Loop / Internal Rack Insert Slot
ae_data.main.N.preins.ins.manualText: Specifies the physical external hardware FX loop or internal software virtual rack slot routed to this pre-processing position on the master bus. This parameter allows you to patch outboard analog outboard gear or digital system mastering processors directly into the final mix path before main processing stages.

ae_data.main.N.send.MX1.on.manualText: Activates or deactivates the specific routing path from this main master channel to the Matrix 1 (MX1) mix bus. Turning this switch to the active position routes the final mix signal into the first matrix mixer block, while turning it off completely silences the feed to Matrix 1.

ae_data.main.N.send.MX1.lvl.manualText: Adjusts the specific send volume or audio signal level routed from this main master fader into the Matrix 1 (MX1) mixer input stage. Modifying this level alters how prominently the global mix is blended into the independent Matrix 1 zone mix.

ae_data.main.N.send.MX1.pre.manualText: Toggles the routing location of the Matrix 1 (MX1) send injection point within the master fader strip. Engaging this switch changes the routing to capture a pre-equalizer or pre-dynamics signal, routing the final mix to Matrix 1 before it undergoes any master EQ or dynamic processing modifications.
