ae_data.main.N.postins.ins.labelText: External Hardware FX Loop / Internal Rack Insert Slot
ae_data.main.N.postins.ins.manualText: Specifies the physical external hardware FX loop or internal software virtual rack slot routed to this post-processing position on the master bus. This parameter allows you to patch outboard analog outboard gear or digital system mastering processors directly into the final mix path after main processing stages.

ae_data.main.N.dly.on.manualText: Enables or disables the delay processing stage for the main master output path. Toggling this parameter to the active state applies the configured time alignment delay value to the audio path, while turning it off completely bypasses the delay processing block to eliminate path latency.

ae_data.main.N.dly.mode.manualText: Configures the operational solo mode behavior and routing priority specifically for the main master output delay module. This setting ensures that time-aligned paths or look-ahead detection windows behave correctly when other sections of the console are isolated.

ae_data.main.N.dly.dly.manualText: Determines the exact amount of time delay applied to the main master output path. This parameter is typically used for master speaker time alignment, aligning secondary zone delays, or compensating for spatial transmission timing gaps in large venue PA setups.

ae_data.main.N.tags.manualText: Stores custom metadata strings or searchable categorization tags for the main master fader path. This allows system engineers and operators to label, group, filter, or instantly recall primary mix paths across the console surface or layout manager based on master output architecture.

ae_data.mtx.N.in.set.inv.manualText: Toggles the phase (polarity) inversion status of the matrix channel input stage. Engaging phase inversion flips the audio waveform 180 degrees, allowing you to correct polarity discrepancies before the signal enters the matrix mixer routing network.

ae_data.mtx.N.in.set.trim.manualText: Adjusts the digital trim gain or attenuation level applied directly at the entry stage of the matrix channel. This parameter allows you to fine-tune and balance discrete input feeds prior to routing them into the independent matrix summing grid.

ae_data.mtx.N.in.set.bal.manualText: Controls the balance and physical width positioning of a stereo source feeding into the matrix mixer channel. Adjusting this parameter shifts the relative level between the left and right components, ensuring precise spatial placement within the matrix zone mix.

ae_data.mtx.N.dir.on.manualText: Activates or deactivates the direct input path functionality for the matrix zone fader. Turning this switch on patches the assigned direct hardware input or external source straight into the matrix bus, bypassing standard intermediate group tracking blocks.

ae_data.mtx.N.dir.lvl.manualText: Controls the individual input volume or clean feed level directed from the direct source connection to the matrix channel summing block. Modifying this parameter establishes the gain weighting of the direct signal within that specific matrix zone.

ae_data.mtx.N.dir.inv.manualText: Toggles the phase (polarity) inversion status exclusively for the direct input feed on the matrix track. Activating this parameter flips the raw incoming direct signal waveform 180 degrees to easily resolve phase cancellation with other shared console buses.

ae_data.mtx.N.dir.in.manualText: Specifies the physical or digital hardware routing patch for the local microphone preamplifier assigned directly to this matrix direct feed path. This parameters links a local input socket into the matrix summing core independent of normal strip flows.

ae_data.mtx.N.col.labelText: Console Strip LCD Backlight Color Index
ae_data.mtx.N.col.manualText: Determines the specific color index used for the physical console strip's LCD backlight display on this matrix zone strip. This parameter allows you to color-code matrix paths (e.g., green for green-room zones, blue for lobby feeds) for instant visual surface sorting.

ae_data.mtx.N.name.manualText: Stores the custom text string used to name or label the matrix zone on the console scribblestrip and digital user interface. This parameter replaces generic matrix numbering with clear, user-defined terms like 'Lobby Feed', 'Front Fills', or 'Cry Room'.

ae_data.mtx.N.icon.manualText: Selects the visual icon index code displayed on the matrix channel's LCD screen. This parameter allows you to assign specific graphical symbols to the console strip, providing immediate visual confirmation of the matrix zone type or output routing target.

ae_data.mtx.N.led.labelText: Physical Control Surface LED Accent Ring Switch
ae_data.mtx.N.led.manualText: Controls the operational state of the physical LED accent ring surrounding the matrix channel encoder on the hardware control surface. This switch toggles the LED encoder ring behavior between standard parameter tracking or custom highlighting modes.

ae_data.mtx.N.busmono.labelText: Global Bus Center-Sum Mono Downmix Rule Switch
ae_data.mtx.N.busmono.manualText: Toggles the center-sum mono downmix rule configuration for this matrix channel. When activated, this switch collapses a stereo or multi-channel matrix configuration down into a uniform monaural signal path using equal center-sum level coefficients, ensuring absolute phase alignment.

ae_data.mtx.N.mute.manualText: Engages the absolute mute override function for the matrix channel path. Activating this parameter instantly cuts the audio signal path at the designated master output stage, silencing the entire matrix zone feed without altering individual bus sends or internal processor structures.

ae_data.mtx.N.fdr.manualText: Represents the exact zone volume or attenuation position value of the physical motorized fader on the matrix control surface. Adjusting this parameter scales the global volume output level of the summing matrix channel and moves the physical hardware fader to match.

ae_data.mtx.N.pan.manualText: The master pan control for the matrix channel path, which allows you to adjust the stereo positioning of the entire combined matrix signal. By moving the pan control left or right, you can alter the spatial placement of this specific matrix mix within the wider physical zone soundfield.

ae_data.mtx.N.wid.manualText: Adjusts the master perceived width of the stereo field for the matrix channel. Modifying this control expands the stereo separation outward for a broader soundstage across the whole matrix zone, or narrows it down toward a focused center point to tighten the output's spatial imaging.

ae_data.mtx.N.mon.manualText: Sets the destination or target bus for the matrix channel's monitor path routing. This parameter dictates where the combined matrix output signal is directed, allowing you to route specific master zone submixes directly to performer headphones, engineering wedges, or local control rooms.

ae_data.mtx.N.eq.on.manualText: This parameter indicates whether the equalizer (EQ) for this path is active. When enabled, the EQ settings for this channel will be applied to the audio signal, allowing you to shape the tonal balance of the monitor mix. The EQ can be used to boost or cut specific frequency ranges, helping performers to better hear certain elements in the mix or to reduce unwanted frequencies that may cause feedback or muddiness.

ae_data.mtx.N.eq.mdl.manualText: Specifies the software emulation model loaded into the matrix zone equalizer slot. This parameter allows you to select between different tonal processing styles for your zone output, including modern transparent digital EQs or classic hardware console emulations tailored for precise room tuning.

ae_data.mtx.N.eq.mix.labelText: Dry/Wet Parallel Signal Effect Blending Percentage
ae_data.mtx.N.eq.mix.manualText: Controls the balance between the original un-equalized matrix signal (dry) and the equalized signal (wet). This allows for parallel equalization across the matrix zone, letting you apply broad tonal shifts while maintaining the raw transient power and natural dynamics of the combined tracks.

ae_data.mtx.N.eq.lg.manualText: Adjusts the fixed gain level for the low-frequency equalization band on the matrix zone path. Modifying this value allows you to boost or cut the bass region of the destination zone, adding structural warmth or carving out unnecessary low-end rumble to match the acoustics of the physical room.

ae_data.mtx.N.eq.lf.manualText: Sets the corner or center frequency for the matrix low-equalization band. This target frequency defines the exact boundary in the lower register where the matrix EQ's low-end gain adjustments will be centered or begin to roll off based on room constraints.

ae_data.mtx.N.eq.lq.manualText: Controls the Quality Factor (Q) or bandwidth response for the matrix low-frequency equalizer band. This setting determines how wide or narrow the frequency bell curve is around the low centerpoint, governing how much sub-bass or low-mid content is affected within the zone mix.

ae_data.mtx.N.eq.leq.manualText: Selects the filter shape or geometry mode for the matrix low-equalization band. You can toggle this setting between a shelf filter curve (which affects all frequencies below the corner point equally) and a parametric bell curve (which targets a localized, specific bass frequency zone).

ae_data.mtx.N.eq.1g.manualText: The gain control for the first parametric EQ band, which allows you to adjust the amount of boost or cut applied to the selected frequency range. This parameter can be used to shape the tonal balance of the monitor mix, helping performers to better hear certain elements or to reduce unwanted frequencies.

ae_data.mtx.N.eq.1f.manualText: The frequency control for the first parametric EQ band, which allows you to adjust the center frequency of the selected frequency range. This parameter can be used to shape the tonal balance of the monitor mix, helping performers to better hear certain elements or to reduce unwanted frequencies.

ae_data.mtx.N.eq.1q.manualText: The Q-factor control for the first parametric EQ band, which allows you to adjust the bandwidth of the selected frequency range. A higher Q-factor results in a narrower bandwidth, while a lower Q-factor results in a wider bandwidth. This parameter can be used to fine-tune the tonal balance of the monitor mix.

ae_data.mtx.N.eq.hg.manualText: Adjusts the fixed gain level for the high-frequency equalization band on the matrix zone. Modifying this value allows you to boost or cut the treble region of the zone mix, adding top-end clarity and brightness or softening collective high-frequency harshness.

ae_data.mtx.N.eq.hf.manualText: Sets the corner or center frequency for the matrix high-equalization band. This target frequency defines the exact boundary in the upper register where the matrix EQ's high-frequency gain adjustments will be concentrated or begin to lift.

ae_data.mtx.N.eq.hq.manualText: Controls the Quality Factor (Q) or bandwidth response for the matrix high-frequency equalizer band. This setting determines how wide or narrow the frequency bell curve is around the master high centerpoint, governing how much upper-mid or extreme high-end content is altered.

ae_data.mtx.N.eq.heq.manualText: Selects the filter shape or geometry mode for the matrix high-equalization band. You can toggle this setting between a shelf filter curve (which affects all high frequencies above the corner point equally) and a parametric bell curve (which targets a localized, specific treble frequency zone).

ae_data.mtx.N.eq.tilt.labelText: Tilt EQ Spectrum Balance Tone Shifter
ae_data.mtx.N.eq.tilt.manualText: Adjusts the Tilt EQ parameter for the matrix zone, acting as a spectrum balance tone shifter around a central pivot frequency. Boosting this value brightens the final mix by raising high frequencies while cutting lows, whereas reducing it warms up the overall output by tilting down the highs and boosting the bass.

ae_data.mtx.N.dyn.on.manualText: Activates or deactivates the main dynamics processor module on the matrix channel path. Turning this switch on engages the configured dynamic processing settings to smooth or restrict the dynamic peaks of the zone audio mix, while turning it off completely bypasses the block.

ae_data.mtx.N.dyn.mdl.manualText: Specifies the software emulation model loaded into the matrix channel dynamics processing slot. This allows you to choose between various compression styles optimized for zone output control, such as clean digital limiters, vintage VCA bus compressors, or optical levelers.

ae_data.mtx.N.dyn.mix.labelText: Dry/Wet Parallel Signal Effect Blending Percentage
ae_data.mtx.N.dyn.mix.manualText: Controls the blend percentage between the uncompressed signal (dry) and the compressed signal (wet) on the matrix zone path. This parameter enables parallel compression, allowing you to heavily compress the mix for density while blending back the raw transients for natural dynamics.

ae_data.mtx.N.dyn.gain.manualText: Adjusts the clean makeup gain level applied at the output stage of the matrix dynamics module. This parameter is used to compensate for the overall volume reduction caused by compression, allowing you to restore or normalize the absolute gain structure of your zone output stream.

ae_data.mtx.N.dyn.thr.manualText: Sets the threshold level for the matrix channel's compressor core. Audio signal peaks that cross above this designated decibel threshold will trigger the gain reduction process, determining exactly at what point the compressor begins attenuating and leveling the zone mix.

ae_data.mtx.N.dyn.ratio.labelText: Dynamics Core Compression Reduction Ratio Multiplier
ae_data.mtx.N.dyn.ratio.manualText: Determines the ratio multiplier used for gain reduction once the matrix zone signal exceeds the compressor threshold. Lower ratios like 2:1 are typically used for gentle leveling, whereas higher ratios or infinity settings convert the module into a brickwall safety limiter.

ae_data.mtx.N.dyn.knee.labelText: Compression Knee Curve Softness Transition Depth
ae_data.mtx.N.dyn.knee.manualText: Adjusts the sharpness or softness of the compression turn-on curve around the matrix threshold point. A soft knee creates a gradual, more transparent transition as gain reduction begins, which is highly desirable for keeping zone leveling musical and smooth.

ae_data.mtx.N.dyn.det.manualText: Selects the methodology used by the sidechain circuit to analyze the matrix zone signal amplitude. Switching between Peak mode (reacts instantly to explosive transients to protect hardware speaker lines) and RMS mode (averages signal energy over time) alters the responsiveness of the compressor.

ae_data.mtx.N.dyn.att.labelText: Dynamics Envelope Reaction Attack Time Constants
ae_data.mtx.N.dyn.att.manualText: Sets the attack time constant, which determines how quickly the matrix compressor applies full gain reduction after the zone signal crosses above the threshold. Slower attack times allow the initial snap of transients to pass through cleanly before compression hits.

ae_data.mtx.N.dyn.hld.labelText: Dynamics Processing Envelope Peak Hold Duration
ae_data.mtx.N.dyn.hld.manualText: Defines the specific hold duration during which the matrix compressor maintains its peak gain reduction status before entering the release phase. This temporary freeze prevents the compressor from modulating or pumping rapidly when handling sustained low-frequency transients across the zone output path.

ae_data.mtx.N.dyn.rel.labelText: Dynamics Envelope Recovery Release Time Constants
ae_data.mtx.N.dyn.rel.manualText: Sets the release time constant, which determines how quickly the matrix compressor stops applying gain reduction and returns to unity level after the zone mix signal drops back below the designated threshold. Careful adjustment of this recovery curve prevents audio pumping artifacts inside the target zone.

ae_data.mtx.N.dyn.env.labelText: Dynamics Gain Processing Expansion Envelope Curve Model
ae_data.mtx.N.dyn.env.manualText: Selects the specific mathematical curve model for the dynamics processor's gain expansion envelope on the matrix path. This parameter modifies how smoothly or aggressively the downward expansion algorithms track signal decay, shaping how the matrix gating or expansion logic handles ambient room bleed.

ae_data.mtx.N.dyn.auto.manualText: Toggles the automatic timing optimization engine for the matrix compressor. When activated, this circuit dynamically evaluates the complex, multi-source material inside the zone mix to automatically adapt the attack, release, and internal thresholds, optimizing response in real time for highly variable summing signals.

ae_data.mtx.N.dynxo.depth.manualText: Determines the maximum amount of signal attenuation applied when the crossover expander or gate module on the matrix bus is fully closed. Also known as the floor range, a lower depth setting creates a subtle attenuation of zone background noise, while a maximum depth completely silences the crossover path.

ae_data.mtx.N.dynxo.type.manualText: Selects the filter profile type utilized within the matrix zone crossover dynamic processor. You can choose profiles such as Low-Pass, High-Pass, Band-Pass, or Band-Reject to isolate specific frequency zones of your zone mix for band-limited expansion or gating processing.

ae_data.mtx.N.dynxo.f.manualText: Establishes the primary centerpoint or split frequency for the matrix bus crossover dynamics module. Adjusting this value determines the exact boundary where the zone mix signal is divided, isolating targeted frequency content for independent dynamic compression or expansion rules.

ae_data.mtx.N.dynxo.q.manualText: Adjusts the Quality Factor (Q) or sharpness of the matrix zone crossover filter band. A higher value creates a narrow, selective frequency window to isolate a single specific resonant band within the zone mix, while a lower value broadens the filter response to encompass neighboring frequencies.

ae_data.mtx.N.dynsc.type.manualText: Selects the filter profile type utilized within the matrix compressor's sidechain detection circuit. You can choose profiles such as Low-Pass, High-Pass, Band-Pass, or Band-Reject to determine exactly which frequency characteristics of the incoming audio will trigger the matrix compressor.

ae_data.mtx.N.dynsc.f.manualText: Establishes the primary centerpoint frequency for the matrix compressor's sidechain filter network. Adjusting this value ensures that the compressor reacts only when specific instrument frequencies (such as low-end boominess or harsh upper-mid buildups in the zone mix) pass through the sidechain filter.

ae_data.mtx.N.dynsc.q.manualText: Adjusts the Quality Factor (Q) or sharpness of the matrix compressor sidechain filter band. A higher value creates a narrow, selective frequency window to isolate a specific resonant frequency buildup, while a lower value broadens the filter response to trigger compression from a wider range of tones.

ae_data.mtx.N.dynsc.src.manualText: Selects the specific input channel or internal bus that acts as the trigger source for the matrix zone compressor's sidechain logic. This allows you to route an external signal to automatically key or control the compression behavior of the final zone mix.

ae_data.mtx.N.dynsc.tap.manualText: Determines the precise location within the source channel's signal path from which the sidechain audio feed is captured for the matrix zone compressor. Options typically include pre-EQ, post-EQ, or post-fader positions, altering how processed or dynamic the sidechain trigger signal will be.

ae_data.mtx.N.preins.on.manualText: Activates or deactivates the pre-processing insert stage for the matrix zone output. Toggling this switch to the active position engages the assigned external loop or internal virtual effect rack slot before the primary matrix processing blocks, while turning it off completely bypasses the insertion loop.

ae_data.mtx.N.preins.ins.labelText: External Hardware FX Loop / Internal Rack Insert Slot
ae_data.mtx.N.preins.ins.manualText: Specifies the physical external hardware FX loop or internal software virtual rack slot routed to this pre-processing position on the matrix zone fader. This parameter allows you to patch outboard analog gear or digital system processors directly into the final zone path before main processing stages.

ae_data.mtx.N.postins.on.manualText: Activates or deactivates the post-processing insert stage for the matrix zone output. Toggling this switch to the active position engages the assigned external hardware loop or internal virtual effect rack slot after the primary matrix processing blocks, while turning it off completely bypasses the post-insert loop.

ae_data.mtx.N.postins.ins.labelText: External Hardware FX Loop / Internal Rack Insert Slot
ae_data.mtx.N.postins.ins.manualText: Specifies the physical external hardware FX loop or internal software virtual rack slot routed to this post-processing position on the matrix zone fader. This parameter allows you to patch outboard analog outboard gear or digital system processors directly into the final zone path after main processing stages.

ae_data.mtx.N.dly.on.manualText: Enables or disables the delay processing stage for the matrix zone output path. Toggling this parameter to the active state applies the configured time alignment delay value to the audio path, while turning it off completely bypasses the delay processing block to eliminate path latency.

ae_data.mtx.N.dly.mode.manualText: Configures the operational solo mode behavior and routing priority specifically for the matrix zone output delay module. This setting ensures that time-aligned paths or look-ahead detection windows behave correctly when other sections of the console are isolated.

ae_data.mtx.N.dly.dly.manualText: Determines the exact amount of time delay applied to the matrix zone output path. This parameter is typically used for aligning satellite speaker clusters, front fills, balcony delays, or compensating for spatial acoustic transmission timing gaps across physical venue zones.

ae_data.mtx.N.tags.manualText: Stores custom metadata strings or searchable categorization tags for the matrix zone. This allows system engineers and operators to label, group, filter, or instantly recall specific matrix outputs across the console surface or layout manager based on venue zones or broadcast logic.

ae_data.dca.N.name.manualText: Stores the custom text string used to name or label the DCA (Digitally Controlled Amplifier) master group channel strip. This parameter replaces generic group indexing with an easily recognizable identifier for operators, such as 'All Drums', 'Backing Vocals', or 'Brass Section'.

ae_data.dca.N.col.labelText: Console Strip LCD Backlight Color Index
ae_data.dca.N.col.manualText: Determines the specific color index used for the physical console strip's LCD backlight display on this DCA channel fader. This allows you to visually isolate DCA master control strips from standard audio inputs or mix output subgroups on the mixing surface.

ae_data.dca.N.icon.manualText: Selects the visual icon index code displayed on the DCA master fader's LCD screen. This parameter applies a descriptive graphical symbol to the channel strip, providing immediate visual tracking of the grouped component family controlled by the fader.

ae_data.dca.N.led.labelText: Physical Control Surface LED Accent Ring Switch
ae_data.dca.N.led.manualText: Controls the operational state of the physical LED accent ring surrounding the DCA master fader's rotary encoder. This switch toggles the illumination behavior between standard relative grouping level tracking and explicit group highlighting.

ae_data.dca.N.mute.manualText: Engages the absolute master mute override function for the DCA control channel. Activating this parameter instantly sends a control command to mute all underlying individual channel paths assigned to this DCA group simultaneously, without changing their independent physical fader coordinates.

ae_data.dca.N.fdr.manualText: Represents the exact volume attenuation scaling value of the physical motorized DCA fader on the control surface. Adjusting this fader proportionally controls and scales the volume levels of all audio channels currently linked to this DCA master group without audio passing through the fader itself.

ae_data.dca.N.mon.manualText: Sets the functional monitoring path assignment rules or target diagnostic bus behavior for this DCA group. This parameter coordinates monitoring priority or console PFL/AFL bus response modes when evaluating grouped input sets from the master control layer.

ae_data.mgrp.N.name.manualText: Stores the custom text string used to name or label the physical Mute Group master button interface. This allows system engineers to customize generic mute keys with identifying descriptions on the control surface, such as 'Band Mute', 'Acoustic Sets', or 'Host Mic Only'.

ae_data.mgrp.N.mute.manualText: Toggles the global master control state for the assigned Mute Group network. Engaging this macro button immediately forces a hardware mute state across all input channels, auxiliary paths, or effect returns that are linked to this specific group index for rapid scene silencing.

ae_data.fx.N.mdl.manualText: Specifies the software or DSP algorithm model loaded into the dedicated effects rack processor slot. This parameter dictates the fundamental sonic engine operating in the loop, such as a studio plate reverb, digital tap delay, chorus modulator, or harmonic exciter.

ae_data.fx.N.fxmix.labelText: FX Total System Dry/Wet Wet Factor Scale
ae_data.fx.N.fxmix.manualText: Controls the total system wet factor scale or dry/wet blend balance inside the effects engine algorithm layer. When running as an insert, this balances the raw direct audio with the generated processing trail; when running on an auxiliary return, it is typically set to maximum wet output.

ae_data.fx.N.pdel.labelText: FX Time-Based Generator Pre-Delay Gap Space Duration
ae_data.fx.N.pdel.manualText: Adjusts the pre-delay gap space duration for time-based sound generators, establishing the exact time offset between the initial raw audio signal transient and the onset of processed reflections or echo generation. This is crucial for maintaining speech articulation before reverb builds.

ae_data.fx.N.dcy.labelText: FX Reverb Space Acoustic Absorption Tail Decay Time
ae_data.fx.N.dcy.manualText: Adjusts the reverb decay time, which dictates how long the reverberation tail remains audible before dissolving into silence. Longer decay times simulate cavernous, reflective acoustic spaces like cathedrals, while shorter decay times recreate tighter, highly absorbent small room environments.

ae_data.fx.N.lc.manualText: Sets the corner frequency for the low-cut (high-pass) filter on the effects return path. Removing unnecessary low frequencies from the wet signal prevents muddy energy accumulation and keeps the global mix defined.

ae_data.fx.N.col.labelText: Console Strip LCD Backlight Color Index
ae_data.fx.N.col.manualText: Determines the specific color index used for the physical console strip's LCD backlight display on this effects processor channel. This allows operators to easily group, sort, and identify active processing blocks across the mixing surface.

ae_data.fx.N.time.labelText: FX Modulated Delay Phase Time Interval Sync Parameter
ae_data.fx.N.time.manualText: Controls the core delay time interval, synchronizing echo intervals or phase modulation offsets to a specified rate. This can typically be adjusted manually in milliseconds or locked to global system tempo clocks for rhythmic tracking.

ae_data.fx.N.mode.manualText: Configures how the effects block handles solo triggers across the console system. This dictates whether the effect return path remains auditioned (Solo Safe) or automatically silences when other console channels are isolated.

ae_data.fx.N.fact.labelText: FX Time Scaling Subdivision Multiplier Ratio Fraction
ae_data.fx.N.fact.manualText: Establishes a rhythmic time subdivision multiplier or fractional ratio relative to the master system tempo. Adjusting this parameter shifts delay echoes into synchronized patterns like eighth notes, triplets, or dotted rhythms.

ae_data.fx.N.pat.labelText: FX Delay Tap Echo Output Geometric Rhythmic Rhythm Pattern
ae_data.fx.N.pat.manualText: Selects the internal geometric or rhythmic routing template for multi-tap delay signals. This setting groups and spaces distinct echo taps to generate complex patterns, ping-pong distributions, or specialized syncopated stereo reflections.

ae_data.fx.N.offs.manualText: Controls the timing offset deviation parameter inside the delay line or modulation network. Modifying this offset introduces minute channel timing gaps, widening the perceived stereo field or adding structural variety to rhythmic tap distributions.

ae_data.fx.N.feed.labelText: FX Processor Variable Feedback Return Regeneration Loop Amount
ae_data.fx.N.feed.manualText: Regulates the amount of output signal routed back into the processor's input loop stage. Increasing this feedback return value generates a higher number of repeating delay echoes or amplifies resonance characteristics within modulation paths.

ae_data.fx.N.flc.labelText: FX Pre-Processor Internal High-Pass Filter Frequency Corner
ae_data.fx.N.flc.manualText: Sets the operational frequency corner for the pre-processor internal high-pass filter. This cuts low-end energy from entering the effects engine core, shielding reverbs and delays from low-frequency rumble before processing begins.

ae_data.fx.N.fhc.labelText: FX Pre-Processor Internal Low-Pass Filter Frequency Corner
ae_data.fx.N.fhc.manualText: Establishes the target frequency corner for the pre-processor internal low-pass filter. This parameter softens high-frequency spikes at the input stage, preventing harsh or piercing transients from exciting delays and reverberations.

ae_data.fx.N.hc.manualText: Defines the fixed frequency cutoff limit for the post-processing high-cut (low-pass) filter. Rolling off top-end frequencies helps emulate vintage hardware decay or warms up modern digital effects returns.

ae_data.fx.N.size.labelText: FX Space Simulator Simulated Enclosure Volume Room Size
ae_data.fx.N.size.manualText: Controls the virtual room size and enclosure dimensions inside the spatial simulator algorithm. Adjusting this modifies early reflection clustering density to construct the perceived physical volume of the simulated environment.

ae_data.fx.N.mult.labelText: FX Reverb Early/Late Room Reflection Scaling Multiplier
ae_data.fx.N.mult.manualText: Adjusts the reflection balance scale multiplier, balancing early structural reflections against trailing dense late reverberation fields. This modifies how front-focused or distant an instrument sounds within the virtual acoustic field.

ae_data.fx.N.damp.labelText: FX High-Frequency Diffusion High Acoustic Absorption Dampening Factor
ae_data.fx.N.damp.manualText: Sets the acoustic absorption dampening factor to control top-end diffusion. High dampening rates emulate soft room borders like wood panels or drapery, accelerating high-frequency roll-off for warmer decay tails.

ae_data.fx.N.xover.labelText: FX Multi-Band Frequency Spectrum Crossover Separation Limit
ae_data.fx.N.xover.manualText: Establishes the explicit crossover frequency split limit for multi-band effects. This separates the incoming audio signal into discrete low and high frequency zones, enabling independent decay, compression, or modulation processing per band.

ae_data.fx.N.mdep.labelText: FX Variable Phase Modulation LFO Modulation Depth Intensity
ae_data.fx.N.mdep.manualText: Controls the low-frequency oscillator (LFO) modulation depth intensity applied across phase or time parameters. Increasing depth heightens chorus thickness, pitch detuning variations, or sweeping filter characteristics.

ae_data.fx.N.mspd.labelText: FX Variable Phase Modulation LFO Modulation Speed Oscillator Frequency
ae_data.fx.N.mspd.manualText: Determines the internal low-frequency oscillator (LFO) modulation speed frequency. Adjusting this scales oscillator movement from slow, sweeping phase enhancements to rapid, shimmering pitch modulation effects.

ae_data.fx.N.diff.labelText: FX Space Modulator Structural Stereo Echo Sound Field Density Diffusion
ae_data.fx.N.diff.manualText: Controls the sound field density diffusion of the stereo echo repetitions inside the virtual space modulator. Adjusting this value alters how quickly individual early reflections and delay taps blend together into a smooth, thick wash of sound rather than distinct, separated echo repeats.

ae_data.fx.N.preset.labelText: FX Algorithmic Block Factory Configuration Preset Identifier
ae_data.fx.N.preset.manualText: Holds the operational factory configuration preset identifier for the loaded effects algorithm block. This lookup index tells the system which core setup data, initial parameter matrices, and routing structures to apply when choosing a specific style of effect.

ae_data.fx.N.load.labelText: FX Algorithmic Engine Reload Initialization Command Flag
ae_data.fx.N.load.manualText: Serves as the internal initialization command flag to force-reload the effects algorithmic engine. Setting this parameter to true triggers a hard reset of all algorithm memory buffers, instantly clearing stale feedback streams and initializing newly modified settings.

ae_data.fx.N.erpdly.labelText: Early Reflections Processing Component Initial Pre-Delay Offset
ae_data.fx.N.erpdly.manualText: Sets the precise initial pre-delay time offset specifically for the early reflections processing section. This establishes the physical time gap between the direct dry transient source sound and the emergence of the first wave of bounding wall reflections inside the simulation.

ae_data.fx.N.ertype.labelText: Early Reflections Acoustic Simulation Environment Target Type
ae_data.fx.N.ertype.manualText: Selects the target environment geometry type for the early reflections acoustic simulation engine. Choosing profiles like Hall, Room, Arena, or Plate instructs the DSP processor to generate specialized wall reflection scattering patterns that match those physical boundaries.

ae_data.fx.N.ersize.labelText: Early Reflections Room Space Boundary Envelope Geometry Size
ae_data.fx.N.ersize.manualText: Alters the virtual envelope geometry size and boundary limits for the simulated early reflection field. Modifying this changes the computed distance between reflective surfaces, adjusting the duration, pattern density, and timing dispersion of the early acoustic spikes.

ae_data.fx.N.erpos.labelText: Early Reflections Microphone Acoustic Position Proximity Pattern
ae_data.fx.N.erpos.manualText: Configures the virtual microphone proximity pattern and physical listening position within the early reflection zone. This setting changes how deep, close, or centered the listening capture node is positioned relative to the source instrument inside the simulated room boundary.

ae_data.fx.N.erbal.labelText: Early Reflections Spatial Left/Right Output Image Balance
ae_data.fx.N.erbal.manualText: Maintains the left and right spatial stereo image output balance exclusively for the early reflections block. This parameter allows you to shift the direct early sound field to one side of the stage or distribute reflections evenly across the main stereo speaker layout.

ae_data.fx.N.erlc.labelText: Early Reflections Input Path Structural Low-Cut Corner Limit
ae_data.fx.N.erlc.manualText: Defines the corner frequency limit for the low-cut (high-pass) filter on the early reflections input feed. This filter isolates the reflection simulation engine from low-end sub-bass rumble, preventing muddy resonances from building up inside the early stage boundary reflections.

ae_data.fx.N.ercol.labelText: Early Reflections Accent Color Frequency Response Weight Curve
ae_data.fx.N.ercol.manualText: Controls the accent color frequency response weight curve applied across early acoustic bounces. Adjusting this parameter shifts the tonal brightness of the initial room reflections to sound either darkly damped or brilliantly bright and reflective.

ae_data.fx.N.erlvl.labelText: Early Reflections Component Segment Output Balance Amplitude
ae_data.fx.N.erlvl.manualText: Sets the master output gain level and amplitude balance specifically for the early reflections section of the reverb engine. This parameter determines how prominently the initial, localized room reflections are heard relative to the raw dry signal and trailing late reverb tails.

ae_data.fx.N.rvtype.labelText: Late Reverb Algorithmic Space Synthesis Mode Geometry Profile
ae_data.fx.N.rvtype.manualText: Sets the geometry profile and computational layout mode for synthesis of the dense late reverb tail. This specifies the core dense-diffusion matrix modeling style used to calculate late tail propagation characteristics like vintage plates, large chambers, or spring networks.

ae_data.fx.N.rvwid.labelText: Late Reverb Algorithmic Field Simulated Stereo Imagery Matrix Width
ae_data.fx.N.rvwid.manualText: Adjusts the matrix width scale for the late reverb's simulated stereo acoustic imagery. Increasing this value opens the perceived lateral dimensions of the late decay tail for wide immersion, while collapsing it focuses the tail toward a tight, monaural center path.

ae_data.fx.N.rvpdly.labelText: Late Reverb Tail Propagation Generation Pre-Delay Block Space Gap
ae_data.fx.N.rvpdly.manualText: Establishes the standalone pre-delay space gap duration applied prior to generating the main late reverberation tail. This creates a controllable pause between the end of early reflections and the onset of dense late decay, leaving breathing room for primary vocals.

ae_data.fx.N.rvbal.labelText: Late Reverb Spatial Image Left/Right Positioning Balance Matrix
ae_data.fx.N.rvbal.manualText: Manages the left/right positioning balance matrix for the dense late reverb signal. This lets you bias the trailing wash of diffuse reflections toward a chosen location in the stereo field or center the sound field uniformly across downstream matrix routing paths.

ae_data.fx.N.rvlvl.labelText: Late Reverb Tail Component Segment Master Output Gain Level
ae_data.fx.N.rvlvl.manualText: Regulates the master output gain level applied directly to the trailing late reverb tail component. Adjusting this value alters the prominence of the dense, fading reverberant wash without shifting the balance of the earlier structural reflections.

ae_data.fx.N.ldcy.labelText: Reverb Multi-Band Decay Scaling Factor Low-Frequency Band Coefficient
ae_data.fx.N.ldcy.manualText: Sets the decay time scaling factor coefficient exclusively for the low-frequency band inside a multi-band reverb algorithm. Raising this value allows the bass decay to ring out longer than mid frequencies, creating dark room weight or acoustic warmth.

ae_data.fx.N.lmdcy.labelText: Reverb Multi-Band Decay Scaling Factor Low-Mid Frequency Band Coefficient
ae_data.fx.N.lmdcy.manualText: Sets the decay time scaling factor coefficient for the low-mid frequency band within the multi-band reverb engine. Adjusting this parameter tailors the resonance duration of low-mid instrumental ranges, helping control boominess or body in the final effect return mix.

ae_data.fx.N.hmdcy.labelText: Reverb Multi-Band Decay Scaling Factor High-Mid Frequency Band Coefficient
ae_data.fx.N.hmdcy.manualText: Sets the decay time scaling factor coefficient for the high-mid frequency band. This parameter regulates the tail length across crucial presence frequencies, allowing you to sustain vocal clarity or contain clutter inside crowded mix buses.

ae_data.fx.N.hdcy.labelText: Reverb Multi-Band Decay Scaling Factor High-Frequency Band Coefficient
ae_data.fx.N.hdcy.manualText: Sets the decay time scaling factor coefficient for the high-frequency band. Modifying this multiplier allows high frequencies to damp out rapidly for vintage tape/room styles, or float cleanly for bright, glistening modern plate tails.

ae_data.fx.N.hsoft.labelText: Reverb High-Frequency Shaving Acoustic Smoothing Softness Filter Threshold
ae_data.fx.N.hsoft.manualText: Adjusts the high-frequency shaving filter threshold to control the acoustic softness of the reverb. Raising this value smooths and rolls off sharp, piercing transients in the high frequencies, yielding a warmer and more balanced reverberant decay that avoids digital glare.

ae_data.fx.N.lxo.labelText: Reverb Internal Triple-Crossover Base Frequency Filter Lower Boundary
ae_data.fx.N.lxo.manualText: Sets the lower frequency cutoff boundary for the reverb's internal triple-crossover filter network. This parameter separates the sub-bass and low frequencies from the mid-range bands, allowing for independent decay and damping control over the lowest octave of the effect return.

ae_data.fx.N.mxo.labelText: Reverb Internal Triple-Crossover Base Frequency Filter Midpoint Boundary
ae_data.fx.N.mxo.manualText: Establishes the central midpoint frequency boundary for the internal triple-crossover network. This setting defines the division line between the low-mid and high-mid frequency regions, isolating specific presence ranges for specialized algorithmic space synthesis.

ae_data.fx.N.hxo.labelText: Reverb Internal Triple-Crossover Base Frequency Filter Upper Boundary
ae_data.fx.N.hxo.manualText: Determines the upper frequency crossover boundary within the multi-band reverb engine. This parameter separates the upper-mid frequencies from the extreme high-end air band, enabling targeted top-end damping and decay configurations without altering the lower registers.

ae_data.fx.N.lshv.labelText: FX Post-Processing High-Pass Low-Shelf Frequency Corner Threshold
ae_data.fx.N.lshv.manualText: Configures the frequency corner threshold for the post-processing low-shelf filter. This control alters the target boundary for low-end frequency adjustments on the wet effect output, making it easy to either boost low-end warmth or clean up sub-bass accumulation.

ae_data.fx.N.lsdmp.labelText: FX Low-End Phase Attenuation Resonant Acoustic Dampening Coefficient
ae_data.fx.N.lsdmp.manualText: Sets the resonant acoustic dampening coefficient used to apply phase attenuation to low frequencies. Modifying this setting controls how rapidly low-end reflections lose energy within the algorithm, preventing dense, muddy resonances from overpowering the master mix path.

ae_data.fx.N.hcut.labelText: FX Output Boundary Dynamic Spectrum Shaving Low-Pass Filter Corner
ae_data.fx.N.hcut.manualText: Sets the corner frequency for the dynamic low-pass filter at the final output boundary of the effects module. This parameter shaves off extreme high frequencies from the wet trail, simulating natural room absorption and helping the processed sound blend smoothly into the mix.

ae_data.fx.N.mtype.labelText: Modulation Engine Phase Waveform Geometry Low Frequency Oscillator Shape
ae_data.fx.N.mtype.manualText: Selects the geometric waveform shape (such as sine, triangle, or random) for the modulation engine's low-frequency oscillator (LFO). This shape dictates the phase-shifting behavior applied to internal delay lines, determining if the modulation is smooth, linear, or complex.

ae_data.fx.N.mrate.labelText: Modulation Engine Speed Phase LFO Base Clock Synchronization Rate
ae_data.fx.N.mrate.manualText: Controls the speed of the phase LFO, establishing its base operational frequency. This rate parameter can be adjusted manually or synchronized with the main console clock, governing how quickly the modulation sweeps through chorus, flange, or pitch-detuning blocks.

ae_data.fx.N.mwid.labelText: Modulation Engine Output Sound Field Phase Matrix Stereo Width Scale
ae_data.fx.N.mwid.manualText: Scales the stereo width configuration within the modulation engine's phase matrix. Increasing this value pulls the modulated effects information out toward the extreme sides of the stereo field for a wide acoustic space, while lower values keep the modulation focused near the center.

ae_data.fx.N.view.labelText: Display Screen Target Focus Component Matrix Active Flag
ae_data.fx.N.view.manualText: Toggles the active status flag for the display screen's component matrix focus view. Activating this parameter forces the console graphical interface to jump directly to detailed parameter sub-menus, charts, or routing maps for this specific effects block.

ae_data.fx.N.shim.labelText: FX Spectral Shimmer High Harmonic Frequency Feedback Generator Feed
ae_data.fx.N.shim.manualText: Controls the level of the feedback feed directed into the spectral shimmer generator. This parameter sends a portion of the pitch-shifted high harmonic trail back through the synthesis loop, creating an ethereal, swelling pad-like effect that follows the source material.

ae_data.fx.N.shine.labelText: FX Harmonic Enhancer Upper Mid-Range Spectral Gloss Presence Intensity
ae_data.fx.N.shine.manualText: Adjusts the upper-mid presence intensity generated by the harmonic enhancer. Increasing this spectral gloss parameter adds an exciting sheen, definition, and top-end articulation directly to the wet effects loop, helping it stand out clearly in dense arrangements.

ae_data.cards.wlive.N.cfg.rectracks.labelText: SD-Card Live Recording Internal Destination Target Track Count Allocation
ae_data.cards.wlive.N.cfg.rectracks.manualText: Defines the absolute number of concurrent audio tracks allocated for live multi-track recording to an installed SD card. Configuring this target count adjusts internal bandwidth and storage buffer frameworks to prepare the system for capturing live inputs.

ae_data.cards.wlive.N.cfg.playmode.labelText: SD-Card Integrated Audio Transport Mechanism Operating Play Mode State
ae_data.cards.wlive.N.cfg.playmode.manualText: Sets the operating playback mode state for the integrated SD card audio transport mechanism. This parameter configures how multi-track files are auditioned from the card, allowing you to toggle between standard workflows such as single track execution, continuous sequence loop playback, or virtual soundcheck routing.

ae_data.cards.wlive.sdlink.labelText: SD-Card Multi-Track Capture Session Stereo Pair Linking Strategy Mode
ae_data.cards.wlive.sdlink.manualText: Selects the stereo pair linking strategy mode used during multi-track capture sessions on the SD card. This rule determines whether adjacent odd/even recording channels are handled as hard-linked stereo interleaved audio assets or isolated as discrete, independent monaural recording tracks.

ae_data.cards.wlive.autoin.labelText: Automatic Input Monitoring Switch Track Input Capture Monitoring
ae_data.cards.wlive.autoin.manualText: Toggles the automatic input monitoring switch for track input capture. When enabled, the console automatically punches the channel monitoring path between the live hardware preamp input and the recorded SD card track return based on the global transport arming and playback state.

ae_data.cards.wlive.meters.labelText: Console Screen Level Meter Display Refresh Update Clock Speed
ae_data.cards.wlive.meters.manualText: Adjusts the refresh update clock speed for the console screen level meter display during multi-track operations. Increasing this rate provides smooth, high-resolution visual tracking of sudden audio transients, while lowering it conserves graphical hardware processing resources.

ae_data.cards.wlive.auto_stop.labelText: Show Controller Automation Target Sequence Session Transport Stop Rule
ae_data.cards.wlive.auto_stop.manualText: Configures the transport stop execution rule for show controller automation tracking sequences. This logic determines if the internal SD multi-track player automatically halts at designated target cues, session boundaries, or specific synchronization timecode markers.

ae_data.cards.wlive.auto_play.labelText: Show Controller Automation Target Sequence Session Transport Play Rule
ae_data.cards.wlive.auto_play.manualText: Defines the transport play initiation rule tied to show controller automation tracking. This parameter dictates how external trigger signals, scene recalls, or sequential production event cues automatically un-pause and execute audio playback from the internal storage drive.

ae_data.cards.wlive.auto_rec.labelText: Show Controller Automation Target Sequence Session Transport Record Rule
ae_data.cards.wlive.auto_rec.manualText: Establishes the absolute session recording start rule mapped to the show controller's automation matrix. This macro command ensures that a live multi-track capture is automatically engaged upon specific cue executions or macro calls, mitigating operator capture omissions.

ae_data.cards.wmadi.mode.manualText: Configures the specialized solo tracking behavior and routing rules for the MADI interface card. This setup regulates how digital incoming and outgoing MADI streaming slots behave when standard inputs or control surface channel blocks are engaged in solo operations.

ae_data.cards.wmadi.rxclock.labelText: External Network Digital Sync Clock Priority Line Lock Active Status
ae_data.cards.wmadi.rxclock.manualText: Displays or toggles the active line lock status of the external network digital sync clock priority configuration. When active, it forces the internal digital audio engine to strictly phase-lock its timing cycle directly to the embedded clock signal on the incoming MADI network stream.

ae_data.play.repeat.labelText: Integrated Audio System Player Loop File Sequence Playback Active Toggle
ae_data.play.repeat.manualText: Engages the file sequence loop playback mode for the integrated digital media player. Activating this toggle commands the system to immediately loop the currently highlighted file or cycle continuously through an active playback directory playlist without stopping.

ae_data.rec.path.manualText: Defines the absolute physical directory destination path or target folder hierarchy on the connected storage drive where all newly captured audio wave records and live multi-track session assets will be written and permanently stored.

ae_data.rec.resolution.labelText: Digital Audio Engine Bit Depth Quantization Processing Format Precision
ae_data.rec.resolution.manualText: Selects the bit-depth quantization processing format precision used by the digital recording engine. Adjusting this value sets the dynamic range limits of the captured audio recordings, allowing you to select between 16-bit, 24-bit, or 32-bit floating point file encoding formats.

ae_data.rec.channels.labelText: Channel Interleaving Geometry Format Layout Count Setup Profile
ae_data.rec.channels.manualText: Sets the channel interleaving geometry format layout count setup profile for live recording files. This tells the system how many parallel discrete audio capture paths are bound together inside a multi-channel container block or written simultaneously across individual monaural files.
